Then the Truth, glorified is He, follows this with what the messengers said in reply to the statement of the disbelievers:

﴿Their messengers said to them: "We are nothing but humans like you, but Allah bestows His favour upon whom He wills of His servants. It is not for us to bring you an authority except by the permission of Allah. And upon Allah let the believers rely." ١١﴾

Thus the messengers made clear to their peoples: "We are humans like you, and the authority we possess is the miracle with which the Truth, glorified is He, singled out every messenger. And the Truth, glorified is He, is the One who bestows grace upon His servants, choosing from among them the messenger suited to each people, and sending with him the miracle that evidences that message. The messenger then conveys everything that Allah commands."

Every messenger acts in this way and proceeds with complete confidence that the Truth, glorified is He, will not abandon him and will give him victory. He, glorified is He, is the One who said:

﴿And indeed, Our soldiers are they who will be victorious. ١٧٣﴾ (al-Saffat).

He, glorified is He, informs us of the reassurance given to the Messenger and those with him at the moment when great events shake them and their hearts reach their throats, and they ask:

﴿When will the help of Allah come?﴾ (al-Baqarah).

Then reports of the Truth's victory for His earlier messengers come to reassure the believers. Here we find the Truth, glorified is He, saying:

﴿And upon Allah let the believers rely. ١١﴾ (Ibrahim).

In this way every messenger declared to those among his people who believed in him that upon Allah alone do the believers rely, entrusting all their affairs to Him alone: patiently enduring the obstinacy of the disbelievers, and trusting that He, glorified is He, gives victory to those who conveyed His message and method, and gives victory along with them to those who believed in the method and the message.

Footnote 1: *yamunn* (يمنّ): bestows and does good. Among the Names of Allah: al-Hannan al-Mannan, meaning the One who bestows favour without boasting of it. Ibn al-Athir said: He is the Benefactor, the Giver, from *mann* in their speech meaning kindness to one from whom no return is sought and who asks no recompense for it. [*Lisan al-Arab*, root: m-n-n].

Next, the Mighty and Majestic relates to us the rest of what the messengers said to their peoples:

﴿And why should we not put our trust in Allah, when He has guided us to our paths? And we will surely bear with patience whatever harm you inflict upon us. And upon Allah let those who trust rely.﴾ (14:12)

We note that Allah, glorified is He, described those who trust (al-mutawakkilun) at the end of the previous verse as "the believers" (al-mu'minun), whereas here He describes them at the end of this verse as "those who trust," because the attribute of faith is implicitly included within the attribute of trust (tawakkul).

We also know that there is a difference between tawakkul (trust in God) and tawakkul in the sense of mere passivity (tawakul, neglect of action). Tawakkul means that one exhausts the means which God has made available, because tawakkul is an act of the hearts, after the limbs have discharged what is incumbent upon them of action and taking up of the causes. So the limbs act, and it is the hearts that place their trust.

The Exalted Lord now brings us the rest of the dialogue between those who disbelieved among the peoples of earlier nations and their messengers, saying:

﴿And those who disbelieved said to their messengers, "We will surely expel you from our land, or you will return to our religion." So their Lord revealed to them, "We will surely destroy the wrongdoers."﴾ [14:13]

Thus we see that when widespread goodness spreads among the people, those who profit from corruption and live off it become angry at it, and the thinking of the corrupters turns to the necessity of expelling the leavening agents of goodness from the land whose people the corrupters live off.

And if the land is too strong for the leaven of goodness, then they must declare their return to the religion of the disbelievers. One does not say "ʿudtu ilā al-shayʾ" (I returned to the thing) unless one was within the thing, then departed from it, and then went back to it.

Now, did the messengers, whom the people of disbelief threatened with expulsion from the land, accept returning to the religion of disbelief?

Of course not. That is why we understand from His, the Exalted's, saying:

﴿Or you will return to our religion...﴾ [14:13] (Ibrahim).

It means (or you will become in our religion).

The messengers did not accept that bargaining, because the Exalted and Glorified Lord sends down the hosts of steadfastness, tranquility and serenity upon the hearts of His messengers and the believers; so the messengers and those with them are not affected by such words.

This is what the saying of the Exalted Lord at the end of the verse expresses:

﴿So their Lord revealed to them, "We will surely destroy the wrongdoers."﴾ [14:13] (Ibrahim).

Thus the heavenly law brings justice, which is the destruction of the wrongdoers, and that is a enduring and perpetual matter of faith forever.

1 Al-millah: the sharia and the religion. And al-millah: the religion, whether true or false. [al-Qamus al-Qawim: 2/236].

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary continues with the promise of Allah, the Exalted, to His messengers and those who believed with them:

﴿And We will surely settle you in the land after them. That is for whoever fears My standing [before Me] and fears My threat.﴾ [14]

Here Allah, the Exalted, affirms that whoever remains steadfast in faith, fears the standing of Allah, the Exalted, fears the Day of presentation before Allah and the Day of Reckoning, and does not turn back (nukūs) from the method of the call to the truth, Allah, the Exalted, will bequeath to him the land of those who disbelieved in Allah. This is the sunnah of Allah, because He, the Exalted, said:

﴿And He made you inherit their land, their homes, and their wealth, and a land you had not trodden.﴾ [27] (al-Ahzab)

We know that whoever fears Allah, dreads Him, and believes that He is the Overseer over every soul, Allah, the Exalted, rewards whoever lives his life in the light of faith by bequeathing to him the land of those who disbelieved. And Allah, the Exalted, said to His Messenger:

﴿And We caused the people who had been oppressed to inherit the eastern and western parts of the land which We had blessed.﴾ [137]

1 Nukūs (نكوص): holding back, drawing back. "Nakasa 'alā 'aqibayh" means he went back on what he had been upon of good. Nukūs means returning backward. [Lisan al-Arab, root n-k-s]

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 14, verse 15:

The Truthful Lord says after that:

﴿And they sought victory (1), and every obstinate tyrant (2) was disappointed.﴾ [14:15]

And (istaftaha) means to seek opening (fath), and there is fath and istifta'. The word (fath) indicates that something closed is opened, and sometimes the word means a tangible matter, sometimes it is figurative, and a third time fath means decision and judgement.

An example of the tangible meaning is the saying of the Truthful Lord:

﴿And when they opened their belongings, they found their merchandise had been returned to them...﴾ [12:65] (Yusuf).

Sometimes fath is figurative, meaning prior good and knowledge, as in the saying of the Truthful Lord:

﴿And when some of them meet others, they say: "Do you speak to them of what Allah has disclosed to you...?"﴾ [2:76] (al-Baqarah).

Likewise the saying of the Truthful Lord:

﴿Whatever mercy Allah opens to the people, none can withhold it; and whatever He withholds, none can release after Him...﴾ [35:2] (Fatir).

As for the example of fath meaning the deciding of a matter, the example is the saying of the Truthful Lord:

﴿Our Lord, decide between us and our people with truth, and You are the best of deciders.﴾ [7:89] (al-A'raf).

Thus we find fath has multiple meanings, all revolving around locks that are unfastened. Fath is ultimately applied to victory, and the example is the saying of the Truthful Lord:

﴿When the help of Allah and the victory come [110:1]﴾ (al-Nasr).

Here the Truthful Lord says:

﴿And they sought victory, and every obstinate tyrant was disappointed.﴾ [14:15] (Ibrahim).

They sought fath, meaning they sought victory, and that was a disappointment for the disbelievers; they sought fath, that is victory, presuming that they had what would grant them victory, and they did this supposing that they had what would support them.

And how would Allah grant them victory while they are disbelievers?

Therefore Allah disappoints their expectation and passes judgement on them with the fate of everyone who lived as a tyrant on earth, arrogant towards the worship of his Lord.

And He says:

﴿And every obstinate tyrant was disappointed.﴾ [14:15] (Ibrahim).

The jabbar is one who compels people to what he wants; and what is meant here are those who are arrogant towards worshipping the Truthful, Exalted Lord, and who are obstinate regarding faith in Him.

1 Istaftahu: sought victory (istansaru). That is: permission was given to the messengers to seek victory (istiftah) over their people, and to pray for their destruction. [Tafsir al-Qurtubi 5/3686]
2 Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir (5/3687): "The jabbar and the 'anid in the verse have one meaning, even if the wording differs; every one who is distant from the truth is jabbar and 'anid, i.e., arrogant."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 14, verse 16:

وماذا ينتظرهم من بعد ذلك ؟

The Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿Before them is Hell, and they will be given to drink of festering pus.﴾ (14:16)

That is: behind the tyrant who arrogantly persists in disbelief is Hell, and what it contains of punishment. In colloquial speech we hear one person threaten another, saying to him, "Wara'ak... wara'ak" ("Behind you... behind you"), meaning by it that he will inflict on him a harm that has not yet come its time.

The word "wara'" (وراء) in the language has several uses. Sometimes it comes in the sense of "after" (بعد), as in the words of the Exalted about the wife of Ibrahim, peace be upon him:

﴿And his wife was standing, and she laughed, so We gave her good tidings of Ishaq, and after Ishaq, Ya'qub.﴾ (11:71) (Hud).

That is: Ya'qub came after Ishaq.

And sometimes "wara'" is used in the sense of "other than" (غير), like the saying of the Truth, glorified is He:

﴿And those who guard their private parts, except from their spouses or what their right hands possess, for indeed they are not blameworthy. But whoever seeks beyond that, then it is those who are the transgressors.﴾ (23:5-7) (al-Mu'minun).

Here the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿Before them is Hell...﴾ (14:16) (Ibrahim).

We know that Hell will come in the future, that is, it is in front of him, yet it awaits him and pursues him.

The Truth, glorified is He, continues:

﴿and they will be given to drink of festering pus.﴾ (14:16) (Ibrahim).

Al-sadid (الصديد) is the thin water that flows from a wound, and it is the pus that runs from the bodies of the people of the Fire when their skins are roasted.

Let us imagine the extent of the pain when one of them needs to drink, and is offered the pus produced from the burning of his skin and the skins of his likes. Pus is something one recoils from seeing, so what of drinking it? We seek refuge in Allah.

1 That is: I marvelled at the guests who brought the glad tidings. It was also said: she had never menstruated, so she menstruated. In the language, "daḥikat al-mar'ah" means she menstruated. Al-Raghib in al-Mufradat denied this interpretation and held that His saying (ḍaḥikat) means she was greatly pleased. [al-Qamus al-Qawim: 1/390]

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on Surah 14, verse 17

Allah, the Exalted, continues, describing what awaits those of them who drink the pus:

﴿He will gulp it down, but will hardly be able to swallow it, and death will come at him from every place, yet he will not die; and behind him is a harsh torment.﴾ [14:17]

"Yatajarra'uhu" (he gulps it down; to take it in sips, one sip at a time): because of its extreme bitterness, it has no smooth flow that could be swallowed easily, so it nearly sticks in the throat. A person does not take something sip by sip unless he is unable to keep drinking continuously. This drink of pus is one that the one who gulps it can hardly swallow. It is said: "istasagha al-shay'" (he swallowed the thing easily), meaning he gulped it down with ease.

His, the Exalted, words:

﴿and will hardly be able to swallow it [yakādu yusīghuhu]...﴾ [14:17]

That is, he can hardly swallow it with ease, because its taste and appearance are unacceptable.

He, the Exalted, continues:

﴿and death will come at him from every place, yet he will not die...﴾ [14:17]

That is, he looks around and finds death encircling him from every direction, yet he does not die. And he is surprised that torment surrounds him from every direction, confirming the words of Allah, the Exalted:

﴿and behind him is a harsh torment.﴾ [14:17]

Thus the arrogant tyrant who obstinately opposes faith is tormented. If we measure the harsh torment against the lightest torment a person may meet in the Fire, we find it is a torment beyond endurance. Indeed the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The least punished of the people of the Fire on the Day of Resurrection is a man on whose soles two embers are placed, causing his brain to boil from them."

So what of the harsh torment? May Allah protect us and you from its evil.

1 *Yatajarra'uhu*: swallowing it with difficulty and aversion (al-Qamus al-Qawim: 1/120). Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir (5/3689): "That is, he sips it little by little, not in one gulp, because of its bitterness and heat."
2 *Sāgha al-sharāb fi al-halq* when it is smooth and easy (Lisan al-'Arab, root s-w-gh).
3 *Al-akhmas*: the sole of the foot and its thin lower part that does not touch the ground (Lisan al-'Arab, root kh-m-s).
4 A hadith agreed upon (muttafaq 'alayh). Recorded by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (6561) and by Muslim in his Sahih (213), from the hadith of al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, may Allah be pleased with him.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 14, verse 18:

He, glory be to Him, then says, after that, a cosmic matter:

﴿The likeness of those who disbelieve in their Lord: their deeds are like ashes upon which the wind blows violently on a stormy day. They have no power over anything of what they have earned. That is the far-reaching error.﴾ [14:18]

There may come to the minds of some people what distorts the beliefs of faith, so they say: How does so-and-so enter the Fire when he is among the most guided of mankind, with those tremendous inventions that changed the courses of civilization and made people happy? How does God punish those who exerted effort to develop the sciences and arts? Does He punish them merely because they are disbelievers?

I say: Yes, God punishes them, despite the fact that He, glory be to Him, does not let the reward of one who does good deeds be lost with Him. He is able to repay them in this world with what they attain of glory, fame and wealth, and they had worked for exactly that.

And his saying applies to them: "I did it so that it would be said, and it has been said" (1). They received their rewards from what they did, for themselves. That is because they worked without God being in their minds.

Thus the Qur'an depicts the matter of recompense. One of these disbelievers, when he suffers the severe punishment for disbelief, the Truth does not deny him (2) the reward for whatever good he did; so he receives it in this world and enjoys having his name attached to his invention or discovery.

We all know his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Whoever's emigration was for a worldly thing he would obtain, or for a woman he would marry, his emigration is to what he emigrated for" (3). As for the Hereafter, punishment is his recompense, because he lived as a disbeliever in God.

These deeds that they performed in this world, which they thought were humanitarian deeds and deeds of righteousness, will come on the Day of Resurrection as ashes which the strong wind blows away on a stormy day, scattering them far:

﴿The likeness of those who disbelieve in their Lord: their deeds are like ashes upon which the wind blows violently on a stormy day. They have no power over anything of what they have earned. That is the far-reaching error.﴾ (Ibrahim).

They will then have no opportunity to resume life in order to benefit from the experience; rather, before them and around them is punishment. The state of each of them says:

﴿My Lord, send me back! So that I may do righteousness...﴾ (al-Mu'minun) [23:99-100].

But if he were returned to life, he would return to what he was forbidden, in confirmation of the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him:

﴿And if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely find better than this as a return.﴾ (al-Kahf) [18:36].

This disbelief is the far-reaching error that made all their deeds, which they thought were righteous, merely deeds that come to nothing; so by disbelief they strayed from the path that leads to the better outcome of the Hereafter.

1 Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih (1905), and Ahmad in his Musnad (2/322) and al-Nasa'i in his Sunan (6/23, 24), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him. Shaykh al-Sha'rawi explained it in his book (al-Ahadith al-Qudsiyya) (1/135-151), edited by me.
2 Ghamat al-haqq (ghamt al-ḥaqq): denying it. Al-ghamt: ingratitude for a blessing and concealing it. [Lisan al-Arab, root gh-m-t].
3 A hadith agreed upon (muttafaq 'alayh). Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (1), and likewise Muslim in his Sahih (1907), from the hadith of Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, and its beginning is: "Actions are only by intentions, and every person has only what he intended."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 14, verse 19:

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿Have you not seen that Allah created the heavens and the earth with truth? If He wills, He can remove you and bring forth a new creation.﴾ [14:19]

Glorified is He, here teaches us that He created the heavens and the earth with the balance of truth, so the sky does not come down and fall upon the earth. He, glorified is He, says:

﴿He holds back the sky from falling upon the earth, except by His permission.﴾ [22:65]

Whenever you walk, you find the sun above you, raised by a precise engineered order.

Thus the Truth, glorified is He, wished to affirm a cosmic matter that is sensed and witnessed, and He began with His saying:

﴿Have you not seen...﴾ [14:19]

Although the sight has no "where" here, since the sun is plainly visible before all people, the meaning of "Have you not seen" here becomes "Have you not known."

He came with ﴿Have you not seen﴾ here to guide us to the fact that what Allah informs us of is truer than what the eye informs us of. So when He, glorified is He, says ﴿Have you not seen﴾, it means: Have you not known with certain knowledge, because your eyes may deceive you in sight, or mislead you in perception; but when Allah says to you ﴿Have you not seen﴾, know that it is knowledge you can rely upon.

When the Truth, glorified is He, draws our attention here to seeing the heavens and the earth, we must know that they could not have come into existence except by Allah's creating them; and He is the One who informed us that they are His creation, and no one claimed them for himself. Thereby the matter of their creation is established for Him, and no one else claims that he created them; no one has ever told us that.

He, glorified is He, said earlier:

﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind...﴾ [40:57]

As we know, no individual human lives as long as the sky lives: the individual dies and another is born; all people come and go, while the sun remains, and so does the earth.

Among the wondrous creation of the Most Merciful is that Allah created all of that subjected to serve man's affairs; no creature among those subjected things deviates from man's affairs.

As for what is demanded of you, O human, as an obligation, you are free in it: if you wish, you believe, and if you wish, you disbelieve; if you wish, you obey, and if you wish, you disobey.

But the creature subjected to serve you does not have this will. He, glorified is He, is the Truth who says:

{We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they refused to bear it and feared it, and man bore it. Indeed, he was unjust and ignorant.} [33:72]

This noble statement has informed us that the mercy of the Most Merciful preceded us, mankind, before our creation, and the mercy of Allah preceded us with a prepared existence for us.

It is wondrous that the universe created for us, to preserve our life and the preservation of our species, is concentrated in things over which we have no control and which never change; namely the lofty things such as the sun, the moon and the earth.

There are other things in which change occurs in two kinds: one kind changes and something new comes in its place, like the plant that goes away and becomes stubble, and likewise the animals we eat or that die.

And there is a creation that changes while its elements remain, even if its substance changes, like the inanimate things we see — the mountains, the earth and its elements — from which we discover something new every day.

So the creatures that received human existence are of two kinds: a kind in which accidents have no role; and another kind in which accidents have a role while its substance remains, namely the inanimate things; and a kind whose types and genera change.

All these things show us that the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, has two attributes:

The attribute of power and subjugation; He, glorified is He, subdues what He wills to whatever He wills, and it does not change.

And the attribute of choice which He placed in man.

The attribute of power by which He, glorified is He, subjected things to serve man establishes His absolute dominion, glorified is He, over every creation; nothing ever departs from His will.

And by the attribute of choice which He bestowed on man, He wished that His servant man would come to Him loving and following His commands of faith; for the one who obeys Allah while he is able to disobey Him demonstrates thereby that he loves Allah, and establishes for Him the attribute of being beloved.

Here the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿Have you not seen that Allah created the heavens and the earth with truth...﴾ [14:19]

We may note that the word "with truth" (bil-haqq) occurs in many places in the Noble Qur'an.

By way of example, we find in the Noble Qur'an His saying, exalted is He:

﴿We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except with truth...﴾ [15:85]

And His saying, exalted is He:

﴿We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them in play.﴾ [44:38]

This shows that the heavens and the earth were created in a fixed form. This has caused the schools of philosophy to receive this matter in two ways: a reception of one who wants to believe, and a reception of one who wants to disbelieve. Those who wanted disbelief split into two groups.

The first group took the stability of the laws of the sun, the moon and the earth as evidence that there is no creator of this universe, and said: If there were a creator for it, He would have changed the form of the heavens and the earth; rather, each of those bodies runs itself by a firm, self-contained mechanism.

The second group of those who wanted disbelief said: the anomalies in the universe and the presence of flaws and congenital defects in some creatures and kinds are evidence that there is no god. How could a god create one creature blind, another lame, and a third with one eye?

Thus this group of disbelievers took the presence of anomaly in the universe as proof of the absence of a god.

It is wondrous that the group that wanted change in the form of the heavens and the earth wanted that as evidence of a creator, while the group that saw anomaly in some creatures took the constancy of creation in one form as evidence of a god.

All this shows us that both groups took two contradictory matters as evidence for disbelief, and the two groups did not agree on one matter, which clarifies the contradiction between them.

If each of the two groups had looked carefully, each would have known that faith is a basic necessity for understanding this universe, both in its constancy and in the presence of some anomaly within it.

So you, who seek constancy in existence, take the constancy of the mechanism of motion in the heavens and the earth, the sun and the moon, as evidence of belief in a creator god, all-powerful.

And you, who take change in creation as evidence of a creator: behold, you see the difference among creatures, which makes you find the non-uniformity among creatures as evidence of a god, creator, who has absolute power.

The Truth, glorified is He, clarified to us that He did not create the heavens and the earth as a game; rather He created them with truth, and there is a difference between a game and truth. A game may be arrived at by one who throws out something, so that a chance result comes out for him which he or someone else uses as a toy.

The Truth says:

﴿He created the heavens and the earth with truth; exalted is He above what they associate.﴾ [16:3]

As for creation with truth, this means that the one who creates them does so by precise, firm measures, and makes them according to a fixed order having a principle governing it of wisdom and truth.

Since the higher universe is stable, it is Allah, the Truth, who created the heavens and the earth; and since you want stability in your voluntary movement, then take the method which Allah sent down with truth, so that your affairs become firm as the higher affairs are firm; and when you depart from the method of truth you will find corruption.

If you want there to be no corruption in society of any kind, then seek the command of Allah which mankind has lost by violating His method, and you will find that its loss is the cause of the existence of corruption. Read His saying, the Truth, in Surah al-Rahman:

﴿The Most Merciful, taught the Qur'an, created man, taught him expression, the sun and the moon by reckoning, and the star and the tree prostrate, and the sky He raised and set up the balance. That you not transgress within the balance, and establish weight with justice and do not make the balance deficient.﴾ [55:1-9]

Thus you see the sun, for example, regulated in its rising, its setting and its eclipse, and likewise the moon in its light, its waning, or its eclipse.

And just as the Truth, glorified is He, raised the sky and set up the balance, so you must weigh every matter by the correct balance so that your affairs are put right, for the balance of material, moral and ethical matters, when upright, is the stability of the movement of life.

But if you persist in crookedness, know that He, glorified is He, is able to remove you and bring forth a new creation:

﴿If He wills, He can remove you and bring forth a new creation.﴾ [14:19]

The literal wording now and its implication are not His intended meaning, because Allah created creation and gave them choice, so that creation would turn to Allah, even though He, glorified is He, has given them the power not to turn to Him.

In another place He, glorified is He, says:

﴿Here you are, those who are invited to spend in the way of Allah, yet among you are those who withhold; and whoever withholds, withholds only from himself. And Allah is the Rich, while you are the poor. And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people, and they will not be like you.﴾ [47:38]

And He says, concerning the Jews' denial of the manner of the birth of Jesus, son of Mary:

﴿And when the son of Mary was cited as an example, behold, your people turn away from it, and they say: Are our gods better, or is he? They did not cite him to you except as a dispute; rather they are a contentious people. He is not but a servant upon whom We bestowed favour, and made him an example for the Children of Israel. And if We willed, We would have made from you angels upon the earth succeeding one another.﴾ [43:57-60]

So then: the absolute power of Allah, which created him without a father, can do whatever it wills, and nothing resists the wills or the powers of the Truth.

And He says in another place:

﴿So I swear by the Lord of the easts and the wests that We are able to replace them with better than them, and We are not to be outdone.﴾ [70:40-41]

No one precedes the will or the desire of Allah.

1 Ashfaqna minha: they feared to bear the trust, and it is among the consequences of not fulfilling its rights. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/351].
2 La'iba: did an action that yields no benefit. La'ibun: playful, not serious. [al-Qamus al-Qawim: 2/194].
3 Al-bayan: speech that expresses what is in the soul of meanings and ideas. [al-Qamus al-Qawim: 1/92].
4 Al-qist: justice. Aqsata: was just and removed injustice and oppression. Al-qistas: the balance and justice. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/116].
5 Al-mihaq: the end of the month when the crescent vanishes and is not seen. Ibn al-A'rabi said: al-mihaq was so named because it rises with the sun and so obliterates it that no one sees it. [Lisan al-Arab, root: m-h-q].

The Almighty says, affirming that His power to bring about a new creation is not an impossible matter:

﴿And that is not difficult for Allah. (Qur'an 14:20)﴾

The word ʿazīz (عزيز, "difficult" or "hard to achieve") means that which is impossible to attain. Allah, glory be to Him, cannot be overcome. He has shown us in the details of life that He takes away a plant and brings another plant in its place, and takes away an animal and brings another animal; likewise He takes away a group of mankind and brings others in their place.

God says, after this:

﴿And they will be brought forth before God, all of them. Then the weak will say to those who were arrogant, "Indeed, we were your followers. Can you then avail us anything against the punishment of God?" They will say, "Had God guided us, we would have guided you. It is all the same for us whether we lament or endure patiently; there is no escape for us."﴾ (14:21)

Al-buruz (emergence) is that something which was hidden appears. It is said, "a man bārz" meaning one who is noticed and gazed upon, and to whom the world opens only on account of him. It is said, "a woman bāriza" meaning a woman who mixes with men and is not veiled.

God says:

﴿And you will see the earth laid bare.﴾ (18:47)

That is, each of us will see the whole earth on the Last Day, complete, not only a part of it as happens in our worldly life. God has indeed said to us:

﴿So We removed from you your covering, and your sight today is sharp.﴾ (50:22)

It is also said "a bāriz horse," which is what is applied to the horse that wins when racing against others, and no other horse can outrun it. Therefore it is a horse that the eye sees clearly during the race.

We know that during the moments of a race, horses raise dust as they compete, that is, dirt that clouds what is seen, so no one sees the details of the place where the horses run. But when a horse appears that outruns all of them, no other horses are near it raising dust that prevents seeing it clearly, standing out and visible.

Here God says:

﴿And they will be brought forth before God, all of them.﴾ (14:21)

One might ask: Were there things hidden from Him, glorified is He, which then emerged?

We say: He, glorified is He, is far above having anything hidden from Him, whether on earth, in the heavens, or in the whole universe. But what is meant here is that they emerge in their own estimation, and they see their existence clearly before God, glorified is He.

They had previously been:

﴿They hide from people, but they cannot hide from God, when He is with them at night, plotting in speech He does not approve. And God is ever encompassing of what they do.﴾ (4:108)

They had thought that they were able to conceal from their Lord what they were doing, scheming and plotting, but on the Day of Resurrection we find them exposed before their Creator. Their judgment in this is the judgment of all creation.

Or: each one of them emerges before himself, and sees himself before God.

We know that He, glorified is He, created creation in two modes: one in which the human is compelled and has no will, and one in which the human is given choice. The proportion of what is given to the human as choice is small compared to what is not within his choice.

God, glorified is He, willed this, because He knew from eternity that the human, who has become accustomed to rebelling against God, is told: you have grown accustomed to rebellion and to saying "No." You may openly disbelieve and fight for it, and want to step outside the wills of the Truth. If you are truthful that this departure is inherent in you, then rebel against the compulsions that overtake you.

Through experience, a person knows that he is not able to do that. The poor man cannot become rich without God's will; the sick cannot be cured without God's will; the weak cannot grow strong against God's will.

All this indicates that God's ownership of you is still by compulsion within you, and a day will come when choice will be taken from you.

﴿To whom belongs the dominion today? To God, the One, the Subduer.﴾ (40:16)

At that moment you emerge with your whole being before yourself, and you find the Truth, glorified is He, before you. Either you will be emerging with all your constituents before yourself at the moment you stand before your Creator, or what is meant by His saying "the Truth" is the standing of all creation before Him, emerging, whether they were followers or leaders.

At that moment we will find His saying fulfilled:

﴿Then the weak will say to those who were arrogant, "Indeed, we were your followers..."﴾ (14:21)

Thus we see that there is a dialogue between two kinds of humans: the arrogant kind, who are the leaders and masters who issue their orders for the weak to carry out; then the weak followers are surprised that their heads on the Last Day are equal with these mighty tyrants, and they see what awaits them all of punishment. So the weak ask the people of tyranny:

﴿So can you avail us anything against the punishment of God?﴾ (14:21)

These arrogant ones had previously been arrogant toward these weak people by their power and dominance, or they were arrogant toward the messengers in faith, as God clarified in another place in the Qur'an:

﴿Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a man of importance from the two cities?﴾ (43:31)

In this statement there is arrogance toward faith, as if they were objecting to God, God forbid, to His will and His vast knowledge by which He chooses the messengers.

Or: they were arrogant toward themselves, so they did not believe; or they were arrogant toward the followers by their status and influence, so the followers could not oppose them. Therefore the followers say to them, at the moment of equality of heads:

﴿So can you avail us anything against the punishment of God?﴾ (14:21)

This is a rebuke, humiliation, and disgrace for the follower.

We know that God said in another place of the Qur'an, in the words of the followers:

﴿Our Lord, indeed we obeyed our leaders and our elders, and they misled us from the way. Our Lord, give them double the punishment and curse them with a great curse.﴾ (33:67–68)

God has presented this matter to us so that we learn from the beginning how the scale of following works. Beware of following in any matter unless you are convinced that it brings you good and repels evil. Let each of us pay close attention and not hand over the reins of directing the movement of life except with clear evidence.

Let each of us remember the Truth's saying:

﴿Like the Shaytan when he says to man, "Disbelieve." But when he disbelieves, he says, "Indeed, I am free of you; indeed, I fear God, Lord of the worlds."﴾ (59:16)

So when an order comes to you that opposes God's method, you must raise God's method above every order. God, glorified is He, has clarified this for us so that we pay close attention and do not throw the reins of our affairs to whom we follow except with deliberation and wisdom: does he guide us to good or guide us to evil, and can he ward off evil from us and save us from being struck by harm?

So let each of us be on clear evidence regarding his affair. God said in Surat al-Rahman:

﴿Then which of the favors of your Lord would you both deny?﴾ (55:16)

Al-ala' (bounties) are blessings. Among the highest blessings are those values God clarified for us so that we walk by their guidance in the worldly life, so that we do not approach life in ignorance, but with explanation and clarification of everything.

Thus the follower should behave toward the one followed so that he does not stand in the shared position of disgrace between the two on the Day of Reckoning, when the followers say to the leaders:

﴿Indeed, we were your followers. So can you avail us anything against the punishment of God?﴾ (14:21)

This Qur'anic statement is spoken by the Lord of the worlds, and every letter in it is for a purpose and meaning.

His saying:

﴿Anything against the punishment of God?﴾ (14:21)

means that they will not be able to lighten even a small part of God's punishment. It is as if they are making it easy for them, asking them to bear it, or to lighten for them even a small part of the punishment.

An example of this is when a person asks another for a pound, and the other says, "I have nothing but this," and the asker replies, "Then give me some of it," even if he was asking for a quarter of it or ten piastres.

Thus spoke those who followed to those they had followed. So what will the response be from those who were defiant toward God in faith in Him? Here they respond to those who asked them to lighten even a small part of the punishment:

﴿They will say, "Had God guided us, we would have guided you. It is all the same for us whether we lament or endure patiently; there is no escape for us."﴾ (14:21)

Thus their lie is exposed. They claim that the meaning of guidance is that God grants them faith, forgetting that the meaning of guidance is the indication that leads to the goal.

For us in God's saying is what clarifies the meaning:

﴿And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance.﴾ (47:17)

Whoever turns to faith with an open heart finds all paths of good before him. But as for one who disbelieves, how would God guide him, when he has preferred blindness over guidance? He will naturally find no guidance at all.

They say this to those they followed on the Day of Gathering, because they see with their own eyes that Paradise is true, Hell is true, and reckoning is true. Therefore they admit before those who followed them in the world that if God had taken them by the hand in worldly life to faith, they would have led you to this faith. In this they are holders of a mistaken opinion.

This is their saying:

﴿Had God guided us, we would have guided you.﴾ (14:21)

We know that when a person falls into a predicament stronger than his capacities, with no gap in it for escape, he meets this predicament in one of two ways. The first way: he laments and implores. The second way: he holds firm and endures.

Here we find the disbelievers saying:

﴿It is all the same for us whether we lament or endure patiently; there is no escape for us.﴾ (14:21)

That is: whether they lament and implore, or endure and hold firm, God will not save them from what they are in. There is no flight and no refuge.

And ḥāṣa in a place means he went here or there and found no rest. In our colloquial expression there is what depicts that, which is our saying "so-and-so is ḥāyiṣ," meaning he finds no place to rest.

Therefore it is said "the earth has rejected them" (nabata bihim al-ard), meaning every place on earth rejects them. God explains this matter, saying:

﴿Until, when the earth became constricted for them despite its vastness, and their souls became constricted for them...﴾ (9:118)

Thus we see that whoever the earth rejects, his own self also does not contain him; rather it becomes constricted upon him. We hear from those whom God afflicts in worldly life someone saying: "I cannot bear myself."

This actually happens to some people in moments of distress: a person's self becomes too narrow to carry itself, as if the one of them has two selves, as if the one of them has two images: the image that adorns desire, and when it exceeds its limit, he returns to the image of one who hates desire. He is not happy in either state: loving desire and hating it.

1 al-Jaza': the opposite of patience, the weakness of the soul in bearing what is disliked. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/122].
2 al-Maḥīṣ: the place of refuge and escape. Al-muḥāyaṣa, a reciprocal form, from al-ḥays, meaning deviating from and fleeing something. [Lisan al-Arab, root ḥ-y-ṣ].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 14, verse 22:

Then Allah, glory be to Him, says after that:

﴿And Satan will say when the matter has been decided: "Indeed, Allah promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you, but I failed you. I had no authority over you except that I invited you, and you responded to me. So do not blame me, but blame yourselves. I cannot help you (mustasrikhikum), nor can you help me (musrikhiyya). Indeed, I disbelieve in your associating me [with Allah] before. Indeed, for the wrongdoers is a painful punishment."﴾ [14:22]

Here we find an escalation in the dialogue. Having been between the leaders and the followers, the dialogue now rises to take place between Satan and mankind. We note that Allah, glory be to Him, here describes the state in which the dialogue takes place: it is the decision of the matter (inqida' al-amr), where the final situation of everything is settled; there is no debate about any matter, and no opportunity to retract what has happened.

The decision of the matter means that every person goes to his destiny: whoever is among the people of Paradise enters it, and whoever is among the people of the Fire enters it. Matters have reached their final limit, after which nothing changes.

Satan exposes himself, saying:

﴿Indeed, Allah promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you, but I failed you.﴾ [14:22]

The promise of Allah is true, because it is the promise of one who possesses (the power to fulfil it). As for the promise of Satan, it is false, because he promised what he does not possess. Therefore his promise is a lie, for the Almighty is the firm reality that does not change.

When you (the human being) promise another person some good to come, do you guarantee that your circumstances will allow you to fulfil this matter for him?

For this reason Allah, glory be to Him, instructs us to say: "If Allah wills" (in sha' Allah) [1], and thereby we return the promise to Allah, for He alone can promise and carry out what He promises.

It is incumbent upon each of us to protect himself from lying, and to say "If Allah wills." If you cannot fulfil what you promised, you have protected yourself from being charged with lying.

We find Satan saying in the Hereafter:

﴿And I promised you, but I failed you.﴾ [14:22]

This is because his promise was vain, and vanity is baseless (lajlaj) [2]. When you judge by it now, the facts will prove the opposite to you, and you will not believe what you had judged.

For this reason, Allah, glory be to Him, clarifies for us the distance between truth and falsehood.

He says:

﴿As for the foam, it passes away as scum, but that which benefits people remains on the earth. Thus Allah sets forth parables.﴾ [13:17]

Thus Satan tries to clear himself, despite his knowledge that he made the promise and does not possess the power to carry it out. Therefore he tries to attach the blame to those who followed him, just like those who said:

﴿If Allah had guided us, we would have guided you.﴾ [14:21]

Then Satan says after that:

﴿I had no authority over you except that I invited you, and you responded to me.﴾ [14:22]

Authority, as we know, is either the authority of compulsion or the authority of persuasion. The authority of compulsion means that one possesses such force that he can compel another to do what he dislikes, while the other is unwilling to do it.

As for the authority of proof, it is that one possesses an argument which makes you act in accordance with what he asks of you and makes you love what you do. Thus Satan acknowledges to mankind on the Great Day of Gathering, saying: "I want to debate with you. Did I have a coercive authority with which I compelled you? Did I have an authority of persuasion with which I convinced you to follow my path?"

"I had no such thing in your worldly life, nor in that (Hereafter). So do not accuse me, and do not make me a scapegoat (shimaa) upon which you hang your errors. I went astray before you and opposed the command of my Lord. I had over you no authority except that I invited you, and you responded to me."

All that I had over you was that I stirred within you the impulses of your souls, and then the impulses of your souls moved, after that, to draw you toward disobedience.

So: Satan either stirs the impulses of the soul, or leaves the soul to move by its impulses toward disobedience, and these are sufficient for that.

I have already explained how sin is recognised, whether it is from Satan as an independent whisper (taswil istiqlali) or a dependent whisper (taswil tab'i). If the soul stops at a particular sin, and the more the person pushes it away the more it insists upon him, then this is what the soul desires from the person, when it seeks one specific sin.

As for the prodding (nazgh) of Satan, it is that Satan moves from one sin to another, trying to lead the person astray. If he finds him refusing one sin, he shifts the misguidance to another, for Satan wants the person to be disobedient in any form; the important thing is that he disobeys. Therefore he tries to enter the person through his point of weakness, and if he finds him strong in one direction, he turns to another.

Satan declares that he is not the one to be blamed for this:

﴿I had no authority over you except that I invited you, and you responded to me. So do not blame me, but blame yourselves.﴾ [14:22]

Thus the one to be blamed here is the one who turned to disobedience, not the one who misled him into it.

Allah, glory be to Him, continues to expose what Satan says to those he misled on the Last Day:

﴿I cannot help you, nor can you help me.﴾ [14:22]

This is the statement of Satan who previously exalted himself over Adam at the moment when Allah, glory be to Him, commanded him to prostrate with the angels. But the situation here is equality between those he misled and himself: he declares that he will not benefit them, and they will not benefit him.

Al-musrikh is derived from the root ṣ-r-kh, from ṣarakha, which means raising the voice so that another hears it, and the one who cries out seeks nothing but help. If someone finds a treasure beneath his feet, he does not cry out; rather he looks around to see whether anyone has seen him or not.

But if a lion attacks him, he must cry out seeking deliverance. Thus crying out has the purpose of seeking help, and this is only possible from one who fears a terror.

And (musrikh) indicates the verb (asrakha), which is a verb to which what is called in the language the "hamzat al-izalah" (the hamza of removal) has been added. The example is the word (mu'jim), i.e., the one who explains the meaning of a word to remove its ambiguity; one says (a'jama al-kitab), meaning he removed its ambiguity, and this added hamza indicates the removal of non-clarity (ujma) from the word.

Also an example of this hamza is the word (atab), meaning he blamed him; when the hamza is added it becomes (a'tab), meaning he removed what caused the blame.

We find in his supplication, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, his noble saying: "To You is the reproach until You are pleased" [3].

That is: if You, O Lord, are displeased with me in anything, then I ask You to remove this displeasure.

Thus we find that removal comes sometimes by adding the hamza, and sometimes by doubling (the letter), as in our saying "the doctor cured his patient (marrada al-tabib mariḍahu)", meaning he removed his illness from him, by permission of Allah.

So: (musrikh) is one who removes another's cry for help. It is as if someone cried out, and someone came to relieve him. Thus Satan declares on the Last Day that he and those he misled are in a dilemma, and that he is unable to remove the cause of this dilemma, nor are they able to remove the cause of his dilemma, and neither will relieve the other.

He adds:

﴿Indeed, I disbelieve in your associating me [with Allah] before.﴾ [14:22]

You associated me with Allah in obedience, when you submitted to my misguidance, and you were not among the sincere servants of Allah, concerning whom I swore by the might of Allah that I would not mislead them. Each of you carried out what I had misled you into; I called you and you responded, and Allah called you and you disobeyed or disbelieved. You became like me, for Allah had already commanded me and I disobeyed.

Allah, glory be to Him, says what comes upon the tongue of Satan to those who disbelieved and disobeyed:

﴿Indeed, for the wrongdoers is a painful punishment.﴾ [14:22]

This is a general principle: the matter of disbelief at its peak. Just as you obeyed Satan and made him a partner with Allah, here Satan informs you of the assessment of this situation, that it is shirk with Allah, and he declares disbelief in this, because the Day of Gathering has come, and in it has been fulfilled the saying of Allah to him:

﴿Indeed, you are among those reprieved, until the Day of the Appointed Time.﴾ [15:37-38]

Before the Appointed Day, which is the Last Day, Satan used to plot, whisper and prod; but on that Day every thing, humans, jinn and all creatures, will emerge before the One, the Subduer, and nothing will remain hidden from the eye.

This is what they deceived themselves with, thinking they could hide what they had done from the eyes of Allah. For this reason we find the sacred hadith saying:

("O children of Adam, if you believe that I do not see you, then the fault is in your faith; and if you believe that I see you, then why have you made Me the least of those who look upon you?")

In your daily life you do not find anyone stealing from another face to face, nor anyone burning another's house before his eyes. If you, O humankind, do not do that to one another, how do you do it to your Creator, disobeying Him?

If you doubt that He sees you, then your faith is at fault; and if you believe that He sees you, then do not make Him the least of those who look at you, for if a person watches you, you would not dare do before him what he dislikes.

For this reason Satan says, acknowledging and confessing that the wrongdoers have a painful punishment, and that wrongdoing at its peak is shirk with Allah:

﴿Indeed, shirk is a great injustice.﴾ [31:13]

When we read this, we either take it as an acknowledgment from Satan, or we understand it as Satan saying:

﴿Indeed, I disbelieve in your associating me [with Allah] before.﴾ [14:22]

Then Allah, glory be to Him, says after it that general principle:

﴿Indeed, for the wrongdoers is a painful punishment.﴾ [14:22]

After Allah, glory be to Him, spoke of the emergence of creation and all beings, then the dialogue between the weak and the leaders, then the dialogue between Satan and those who disbelieved and disobeyed, He brings the final judgment:

﴿Indeed, for the wrongdoers is a painful punishment.﴾ [14:22]

[1] Referring to His saying: ﴿And never say of anything, "Indeed, I will do that tomorrow," except [when adding] "If Allah wills."﴾ [18:23-24]
[2] Lajlaja: for a man to speak in an unclear manner. Lajlaja and talajluj: hesitation in speech. Al-lajlaj: that which is mixed and not straight. Al-haqq is ablaj, i.e., bright and straight. [Lisan al-Arab, root l-j-j]
[3] Ibid., root j-f-' ... (see note on the Prophet's supplication after the people of al-Ta'if harmed him).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 14, verse 23:

Circumstances (al-munasabat) suggest their counterparts, so that the soul is eager and receptive to this counterpart, as in the words of the Truthful One, glory be to Him:

﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss﴾ (al-Infitar, 13).

Following it comes its counterpart:

﴿And indeed, the wicked will be in the Hellfire﴾ (al-Infitar, 14).

Just as He brought the counterpart of the wretched, it is necessary that He open hearts to enjoy the happy destiny and recompense of those who were made happy by faith.

Therefore the Truthful One, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And admit those who believed and did righteous deeds into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever by the permission of their Lord. Their greeting therein will be, "Peace."﴾ (23)

Here the verb appears, and it can be attributed to three directions. Each direction has a particular point of observation. Sometimes the verb is ascribed to God, glory be to Him; sometimes it is ascribed to the angels who receive the command from God to admit the believers into Paradise; and sometimes to the believers who enter Paradise by God's permission.

So God admitted them by permission, the appointed angels opened the gates of Paradise for them, and the believers entered in actuality.

Thus each point of observation has its own meaning.

There is another reading of the verse that clarifies this:

(And admit(1) those who believed and did righteous deeds into Paradise), and the speaker here is God. We observe that God said here:

﴿And admit those who believed and did righteous deeds into gardens...﴾ (Ibrahim, 23).

The word "admit" (adkhala) implies that He, glory be to Him, permitted their entry, because He said in the same verse:

﴿by the permission of their Lord﴾ (Ibrahim, 23).

And that the angels charged with this opened its gates for them, and the believers entered it—all of this by God's permission.

We observe that all the discussion here is about "gardens" (jannat), so what are the gardens? We say: the root meaning of jannah (garden) is concealment (al-sitr), and from it comes junun (madness), meaning concealment of the intellect. The root is jim and nun, and the garden conceals whoever is in it with its many trees, so that one who walks in it is not seen, because its trees conceal him.

Or: whoever enters it sits in it and no one sees him, because every good in it does not compel him to leave it.

The term "gardens" is also applied to what is in this world, and the Truthful One, glory be to Him, said:

﴿Would any of you like to have a garden of palms and grapevines...?﴾ (al-Baqarah, 266).

We should know that the garden is other than the dwellings within the garden, because the Truthful One, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And good dwellings in gardens of perpetual residence...﴾ (al-Tawbah, 72).

The garden—and to God belongs the highest likeness—is the wide enclosure, and this breadth is distributed over every sight of the eye. Man—with the wonders of his creation—loves to be secluded in one place at times, and loves to spread out in another place at other times, so he rents an apartment or builds for himself an independent house (a villa). In the house or villa, a person loves to have a private room that no one else enters.

People evaluate things on this basis: one who wishes to buy a plot of land to build a house on looks at whether it overlooks an alley or a street, whether he will be able to build several storeys or not, and whether he will set aside a piece of the land as a garden or not.

If the land overlooks open space, then the value of the meter is not measured by the price paid for it, but by the value of the expanse of horizon and open space it offers, such as farms or the sea, for example, where no one will intrude upon you in that place.

The gardens, in this approximate form, are spacious places, and everyone who enters them has good dwellings in them; those gardens have rivers flowing beneath them.

And those who enter them:

﴿abiding therein forever by the permission of their Lord﴾ (Ibrahim, 23).

This is because a person loves enjoyment, but every worldly enjoyment has something that spoils it, and whether it lasts or does not last. Each of us has seen people who lived in bliss, then it was taken from them by the turning of circumstances, or they left it by the decree of death.

As for the garden of God and its bliss, the matter is different, because the bliss there does not escape you, nor do you escape it, for it is according to the capacity of your Lord.

We observe that the words of the Truthful One, glory be to Him:

﴿abiding therein forever﴾ (Ibrahim, 23).

clarify that abiding in Paradise is everlasting by God's permission.

He, glory be to Him, continues:

﴿Their greeting therein will be, "Peace."﴾ (Ibrahim, 23).

Greeting (tahiyyah) is what one person offers another to affirm his joy at meeting him; therefore the greeting corresponds to the measure of joy. Sometimes the greeting is merely raising the hand without a handshake, and one may not be content with that when the esteem one has for one's companion increases, so one shakes his hand, and may even embrace him, and thus one ascends in greeting, and it is a declaration of joy at the meeting.

The greeting of Paradise is peace (salam), because peace is the security of every person: peace with yourself, so that you do not disturb it with inner speech that regrets what has passed, or dreams of something to come. In Paradise you will find no disturbances from the past, the present, or the future, and you will be in harmony with everything around you in the universe: the inanimate, the plants, humans, and the angels.

Therefore the Truthful One, glory be to Him, said, as a conclusion to this verse:

﴿Their greeting therein will be, "Peace."﴾ (Ibrahim, 23).

This is the best blessing, which is life in peace and security. After that, the angels enter upon them, in confirmation of the words of the Truthful One, glory be to Him:

﴿And the angels will enter upon them from every gate, [saying], "Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured. Excellent is the final attainment of the home."﴾ (al-Ra'd, 23-24).

Then they are greeted with the supreme peace from God, who said:

﴿Peace, a word from a Lord Most Merciful﴾ (Ya-Sin, 58).

1 This is the reading of al-Hasan (wa-udkhila) in the form of the future-passive/resumptive, as stated by al-Qurtubi in his tafsir (5/3996).

2 Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: They enter upon them three times each day of the days of this world, bringing with them gifts from God that they did not have in the gardens of Eden. [al-Durr al-Manthur 4/639].

3 On the authority of 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "None of you performs ablution, completing or perfecting the ablution, then says: 'I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is the servant and Messenger of Allah,' except that the eight gates of Paradise are opened for him, and he may enter by whichever of them he wishes." Related by Muslim in his Sahih (224).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 14, verse 24:

Having explained the states of those near to God and prosperous, and those far away and wretched, God, glorified is He, wished to set forth for us a parable that makes clear the difference between the path of the happy, who lived by God's method, and the path of the wretched, who followed various methods other than God's method. So He, glorified is He, said:

﴿Have you not considered how Allah presents an example: a good word is like a good tree, whose root is firmly fixed and whose branches are in the sky, 24 giving its fruit at every time by the permission of its Lord. And Allah presents examples for the people that perhaps they may remember. 25﴾

The mathal (parable, example) is that which clarifies the hidden by means of the manifest. You say to a friend of yours: "Have you seen so-and-so?" He says to you: "No, I have not seen him." So you say to him: "He resembles our friend so-and-so." Thus you clarify, for your friend's imagination, the one who is hidden from it by means of one whose image is clear in his imagination.

Al-Haqq (the Truth), glorified and exalted is He, presents examples to us by means of perceptible matters, so that He may convey the meanings to our minds, because man is accustomed to the perceptible, and the perceptions of his senses first give him perceptible matters, then the meanings are established for him afterwards.

The Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿Indeed, Allah is not ashamed to present an example: a mosquito or what is smaller than it.. 26﴾ (al-Baqarah).

The disbelievers said: "Would Allah present as an example a mosquito?" That is because they did not know that the mosquito has life, and in it there is movement like any living creature, and its anatomical structure resembles the anatomical structure of all living beings in detail, and it performs all the vital functions required of it.

No one other than those who study the science of insects can know how it breathes, or how it digests its food, nor how a circulatory system exists in it, nor the location of its specific glands, and it is an insect of minute craftsmanship.

He, glorified is He, presented many examples in order to clarify the hidden matter by means of the manifest matter. Afterwards the mathal spreads among people, and we say: the word (ḍaraba) is like (ḍaraba al-'umlah, "striking the currency"), and the people formerly used to bring pieces of silver or gold and shape them with a specific measure and form to indicate a value, and thereby they become a circulating currency. It is also said: "ḍuriba fī Miṣr" (it was struck in Egypt), meaning: it was approved and became a established fact. Likewise the mathal, when it spreads and becomes an established fact.

The mathal which the Truth, glorified is He, presents here is the good word, and it has four characteristics:

﴿like a good tree.. 24﴾ (Ibrahim).

That is: it gives you goodness in which your soul finds rest, whether as a sight, a fragrance, or fruit, or all of these together. So His saying:

﴿like a good tree.. 23﴾ (Ibrahim).

suggests that all the senses find in it what gives them comfort, and the word (ṭayyibah, good) is derived from goodness across all means of sensation.

The first characteristic is that it is a good tree. As for the second, its root is firmly fixed, like the faith of the loving believer. The third is that its branches are in the sky, and this is also evidence of the firmness of the root and the goodness of its origin.

As for the fourth characteristic, it gives its fruit at every time by the permission of its Lord, that is: in it is the giving of provision that knows neither limit nor number. And it indicates the qualities of the loving believers.

Since it is a good tree, it is a plant organism that must be nourished in order to preserve the elements of its life. The elements of a plant's life are found in the earth, and if the tree is loose and not firmly fixed, it will not be able to take its nourishment.

Therefore the Truth, glorified is He, says about that tree:

﴿whose root is firmly fixed and whose branches are in the sky.. 24﴾ (Ibrahim).

We all think that the tree takes its nourishment only from the roots; but the scientific fact confirms that the tree takes five percent of its nourishment through the roots, and the rest it takes from the air, and whenever the air is clean, the tree grows with the utmost energy it has, until its branches almost reach the sky.

But if the environment is unclean and polluted, the air becomes unclean to a degree that does not allow the tree to grow the appropriate growth, so unsuitable influences pass over the tree, and it does not extract from them the appropriate nourishment, nor does it grow the appropriate growth.

Except if rain falls upon it and washes its leaves.

Therefore, the saying of the Truth, glorified is He:

﴿whose root is firmly fixed.. 23﴾ (Ibrahim).

means: it takes from the earth.

And His saying:

﴿and whose branches are in the sky.. 24﴾ (Ibrahim).

shows that it takes from above.

¹ Asl al-shay' (the root of a thing): its foundation and base upon which it stands and which is at its bottom. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/21].
² Al-ukul (the fruit): the fruit of the palm and trees, and everything that is eaten is ukul. [Lisan al-'Arab, entry: akl].

Continuing, He (glory be to Him) says:

﴿It gives its fruit every season, by the permission of its Lord.﴾ (Ibrahim 25)

Al-ukul (الأُكُل) is that which is eaten and enjoyed. But we do not take the meaning here as only that which is eaten by the mouth, for there are good trees and plants because the general temperament of the universe requires them. Shade, for example, is benefited from, and likewise there are trees whose very existence interacts with the air (al-athir) and takes from it a pleasant fragrance.

The example of this: a Bedouin child saw his neighbours' palm trees bearing dates, while the palm tree they owned bore no fruit. He wondered why, and went to cut it down. His father caught up with him and prevented him, and said to him: "Our palm is the male which produces the pollen necessary for the rest of the palms so that they may bear fruit."

Therefore I do not agree with those commentators who went to interpret His saying, the Truth:

﴿like a good tree﴾ (Ibrahim 24)

as meaning that it is like the apple tree and other fruit-bearing trees. For every tree, even the colocynth tree, is good through its benefit which the Truth has deposited in it. The colocynth tree gives us a medicine, which may be bitter in taste, yet it cures some diseases by God's permission.

For everything described as a tree has a good function in this universe. And the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him:

﴿It gives its fruit every season﴾ (Ibrahim 25)

indicates that there is a common measure shared by all trees, whether they bear fruit that we see or otherwise.

Modern science has alerted us that every green plant purifies the air by taking in carbon dioxide and adding oxygen to us, and the greenery continues to do this by day, and reverses its role by releasing carbon dioxide and absorbing oxygen at night, as if it were programmed to understand that day requires movement.

The living being needs more fuel for movement, which is oxygen, and a human being during movement consumes a large quantity of oxygen; we find one who climbs a staircase gasping, because his lungs are trying to absorb the greatest possible amount of oxygen to oxidize the blood and produce the energy necessary for climbing. Thus we find that every green plant performs specific functions previously determined for it by the Supreme Creator.

Therefore the scholars differed in interpreting:

﴿It gives its fruit every season﴾ (Ibrahim 25)

Some said: "al-hin" (الحين) applies to a moment, such as the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him:

﴿Then why, when it [the soul] reaches the throat (al-halqum)¹ [83], and you at that time are looking on [84]?﴾ (al-Waqi'a)

Another commentator said: "al-hin" is meant as morning and evening, and the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿So glorify God when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning…﴾ (al-Rum 17)

I say: Let us note that "al-hin" is the time when what is decreed arrives. If "al-hin" is the moment the soul reaches the throat, then this moment is what is meant by "al-hin" here; and if what is intended is a longer period than that, morning and evening, then this period also falls under the meaning of al-hin.

And the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿and the patient in misfortune and adversity and at the time of battle…﴾ (al-Baqara 177)

Al-ba'sa' means war, and the duration of war may be long. Likewise He says:

﴿And for you on earth is a dwelling place and enjoyment for a time [hin]﴾ (al-A'raf 34)

Thus the meaning of "al-hin" here is an unspecified term that extends until the earth is changed into other than the earth and the heavens into other than the heavens. So there is no fixed time-span by which we can define the meaning of "al-hin".

The Truth, glory be to Him, concludes the noble verse that is the subject of our reflections with His saying:

﴿And God sets forth parables for people, that they may remember﴾ (Ibrahim 25)

Striking a parable (darb al-mathal) means presenting something small to indicate something great, or something manifest to indicate something hidden, in order to bring abstract meanings close to the first means of perception, which are the perceptions of the senses: hearing, sight, and the rest of the means of perception.

When meanings that suit the rational aspiration come, a person passes beyond the stage of the senses to abstract knowledge; so the Truth, glory be to Him, brings them close by striking parables for us that convey the meaning He wishes to convey.

The Truth, glory be to Him, does not shy away, as He said, from striking a parable with a gnat and what is above it². Some orientalists say: "Why did He not say 'and what is below it'?"

We say to whoever says that: you have not understood the Arabic language, and therefore you have not received the Qur'an with the Arab faculty of speech, for a parable is struck with the fine thing, and what is above the fine is the finer.

The Truth, glory be to Him, strikes for us the parable of the life of this world, which is the life from the time God created man, for there were other species before man. Here He, glory be to Him, clarifies for us by parable what pertains to life from the moment of the creation of Adam until the Hour is established. He folds it up — that long, wide life spanning the lifetimes of generations — and gives it to us in the form of a concise parable. He says to us:

﴿And set forth for them the parable of the life of this world: it is like water which We send down from the sky, and the vegetation of the earth mingles with it, then it becomes dry stalks which the winds scatter. And God is ever Able to do all things﴾ (al-Kahf 45)

Thus the Truth, glory be to Him, folds all of life into this parable of water that descends and plants that grow until they ripen, then the winds scatter them³.

Likewise the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Know that the life of this world is only play and amusement, adornment and boasting among you, and rivalry in wealth and children. It is like rain whose vegetation pleases the disbelievers; then it dries up and you see it turning yellow; then it becomes debris…﴾ (al-Hadid 20)

Thus the Truth, glory be to Him, folds the life of this world in its length and breadth into this simple parable, so that we see what clarifies for us the hidden meanings in a sensible form, such that the natural intellect can grasp what God wants from it.

We know that sensible things are perceived first, then one ascends to the level of imagination (takhayyul), then comes conception (tawahhum). The stages of perceiving hidden things are: sense first; then imagination second; then conception third.

Imagination (takhayyul) is to combine a whole that has no existence outside, even if it is composed of matter and things that exist outside. An example of this is the saying of a poet who wanted to describe the tattoo on his beloved's hand, saying:

*A pearl-diver's [...] whose fingers in its design are the tattoo of chain-mail*
*A fish of crystal in a net woven of chrysolite*

When you search for the whole image in these verses of poetry, you will not find it existing in reality; but the poet created it from components and elements that exist in reality. The fish exists and is known, the crystal exists and is known, likewise the net and the chrysolite; and the poet wove that non-existent image from things that actually exist. This is imagination, which brings the meaning close.

Conception (tawahhum) differs from imagination. If imagination is forming an image not existing in reality from elements that exist in this reality, then conception is an image not existing in reality, composed of elements that do not exist in this reality.

The Truth, glory be to Him, says to us about Paradise:

﴿And therein is whatever the souls desire, and delightful to the eyes…﴾ (al-Zukhruf 71)

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) explains this with an explanatory note, saying: "Therein is what no eye has seen, nor ear has heard, nor has it occurred to a human heart."⁴

The eye is a means of perception and sensation, and so is the ear; but what does not occur to the heart is for imagination or conception to explain.

Thus we know why God strikes parables for us: to summarize for us what is explained and clarified by things close to human understanding.

When you want to write to a friend, you may take up paper and pen and compose a long letter; but if you have time, you will try to concentrate all meanings into a few words.

We all recall what Sa'd Zaghloul⁵, leader of the 1919 Egyptian revolution, wrote to one of his friends after composing for him a letter of five pages; he ended it: "I apologize for the length of the address, for I did not have time to be brief." For whoever is brief places many meanings in few words.

When a Muslim commander requested support from Khalid ibn al-Walid, while the commander requesting help was besieged, he sent Khalid two words: "Only you I want" (إياك أريد), and thus the besieged commander condensed what he wished to convey to the one who would rescue him, with great brevity.

The poet says:

*When God wills to spread a virtue*
*that has been concealed, He lets a envious tongue make it known*
*Were it not for the fire kindled by what is beside it,*
*the fragrance of the oud's scent would not be known.*

That is: if there is a hidden virtue forgotten by people, then the Truth, glory be to Him, allows a hateful, spiteful envious tongue to chatter, dig and search, so that it appears and becomes manifest, just as oud wood — one of the finest kinds of incense — is placed in fire, and its fragrance spreads among people.

Thus the poet struck a parable to clarify a matter for the reader or listener.

And the poet, also striking a parable, says:

*When a man praises another for his gift*
*and prolongs it, he has prolonged his satire.*
*Had the distance to the water in the well not been measured,*
*he would not have lengthened his rope when it came to drawing.*

Common standards say: when a man praises someone for a long time, this means elevation and glory for the one praised. But when someone reads this poet's words, he may marvel and be astonished; yet he pauses at the poet's words that if the water were near in the well, the thirsty one would draw it with a bucket tied to a short rope, but if the water is at a distance in the well, this requires a long rope for the bucket to reach the water.

This means that prolonged praise expresses the coarseness of the one praised, who responds only to lengthy praise; had the one praised been truly generous, he would have been content with a word or two in his praise.

Thus striking a parable is a clarification and bringing close to the mind.

Here the Truth, glory be to Him, said:

﴿And God sets forth parables for people, that they may remember﴾ (Ibrahim 25)

Remembrance means that something was known by innate nature, but heedlessness came upon it, so the parable comes to remind of the innate matter.
