Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 14, verse 26:

After Allah, glory be to Him, had set forth the parable of the good word as a clarification of the state of those who draw near to Allah, have affection for Him, and follow His methodology, He wished to mention the opposite, which is the state of the wretched who turned away from Allah and from His methodology. So He, glory be to Him and exalted, says:

﴿And the likeness of an evil word is like an evil tree, uprooted from the surface of the earth, having no stability.﴾

When we compare the evil word with the good word, we discover the vast difference. The evil word is uprooted from the surface of the earth. And the *juththah* (corpse), as we know, is the body from which the soul has departed. After it becomes a corpse, it becomes *rimmah* (decayed bones), and then it decomposes into its original elements.

Thus, *ijtith'ath* (uprooting) is the removal of a thing from its origin and its pulling out from its roots, whereas the counterpart in the good tree is that its root is firm, not loosened by circumstances or events. The evil word has no roots because it is uprooted, and it has no *qarar* (place of stability) in which to settle.

When the exegetes spoke about the good tree, some of them said it is the palm tree, because everything in it is good: its leaves do not fall, it remains always as shade, and everything in it is benefited from.

For example, we take the trunk of the palm and make from it pillars for houses in the countryside; we make chairs from its fronds (*jarid*); we take the fibre (*layf*) found between its branches to make ropes; and we make baskets (*qufaf*) from its palm leaflets (*khawas*).

As for those who tried to interpret the "evil tree" as the colocynth tree (*hanzal*), or the fig tree, or the *kurrat* tree, to all of these I say: Allah, glory be to Him, created it to be a good tree in the circumstances where we need it. For when you look at the universe, you will find that its natures are diverse, and the requisites of life are not only food and drink. Rather, there is an ecological balance which the Exalted Truth has designed, and He is the One most knowing of us all about what He created, and He created nothing but good.

Everything in the universe has continuous bounty that radiates into the air, and the example of that is the falling of tree leaves, which restore fertility to the earth once more.

All these are matters which Allah, glory be to Him, *yubdi* (manifests) and does not *yabtadi* (originate), meaning He makes them appear after they had existed eternally and were hidden from us.

He, may He be exalted and high, raises some people and lowers others, and He is the One who said of Himself:

﴿Every day He is in a matter.﴾ (al-Rahman)

We all know that the day in a certain region begins at a certain time and ends at a certain time, and geographical regions differ, and with them the beginnings of any day differ from one region to another. So after a moment from the beginning of your day, another day begins in another region, and thus the days and the beginnings of night and day multiply among the various peoples and societies.

Therefore, when we hear the saying of the Messenger (ﷺ): "Indeed Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, extends His hand at night to accept the repentance of the one who sinned by day, and He extends His hand by day to accept the repentance of the one who sinned by night, until the sun rises from the west."

The meaning of that is that the outstretched hand of Allah is constant, for the night begins at every moment for one people, and the day begins for another people at the same moment, and the succession of night and day follows the rotation of the sun around the earth.

Thus we must not wrong the garlic tree, or the colocynth tree, or any tree among the creatures of Allah, and describe them as an evil tree. For nothing among the creatures of Allah is evil.

When we see a young man bending a piece of iron, an ignorant person may think he is misusing the iron, but the intelligent person knows that he is bending it to make from it what benefits him, like a hook (*khuttaf*) with which he pulls something he needs.

The pillar of the good word is the testimony (*shahadah*) "There is no god but Allah, and Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah," and from this testimony all good branches out. From here we know that the pillar of the evil word is disbelief in that testimony, and what follows disbelief of obstinacy against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), turning away from the way of Allah, denial of the miracles of the messengers, and rejection of the methodology of Allah.

One might say: since Allah, glory be to Him, has said that there is an evil tree, then that tree must exist. I say: everything that harms a person at a certain time is evil. Sugar, for example, is evil for a diabetic. Every creature has beneficial qualities and a harmful aspect in certain conditions, and the chooser (human being) must distinguish what harms him from what benefits him.

We note here, in the description of the evil word as an evil tree, that Allah, glory be to Him, did not say that this evil tree has a branch in the sky, because it is uprooted from the earth, its roots loosened. It has no support from the earth, and no supply from the sky.

Therefore Allah, glory be to Him, describes it:

﴿It has no stability.﴾ (Ibrahim)

That is: it has no permanence or standing. Likewise is disbelief in Allah: whoever disbelieves, no good deed ascends for him, for there is no foundation by which a good deed or good word may ascend.

For this reason the evil tree is described with three attributes: first, that it is an evil tree; second, that it lacks origin and stability; and third, that it has no stability because its origin is not firm.

Then Allah, may He be exalted, explains, speaking of the harvest of the two states: the first is security and safety in this world and the Hereafter; the second is wrongdoing with misguidance, and anxiety with constriction, and in the Hereafter, for them, a painful punishment.

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on Surah 14 (Ibrahim), verse 27

He, glorified and exalted is He, says:

﴿Allah keeps firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter, and Allah leads astray the wrongdoers, and Allah does what He wills.﴾ (27)

The word "tathbit" (steadfastness, making firm) comes naturally here after His saying:

﴿Uprooted from above the earth, having no stability.﴾ (26) (Ibrahim)

For that which is uprooted has no firmness and no stability, so the counterpart is given in His saying:

﴿Allah keeps firm those who believe...﴾ (27) (Ibrahim)

The word "tathbit" also suggests that man is a son of changing circumstances (aghyar, that which is subject to change), and events befall him which are the result of the choices of the responsible persons in carrying out a ruling or annulling it. The responsible person, when Allah commands him with a ruling, may carry it out, and may not carry it out.

Likewise, the responsible person may encounter one who opposes the method of Allah, so this opponent does not implement the teachings of the method, and harms those who follow the teachings. Here the believer is confident that he has a God who will not forsake him in facing those circumstances, and He will help him, whether near or far, against that.

Thus events do not overcome the believer, and His true saying is fulfilled:

﴿Allah keeps firm those who believe...﴾ (27) (Ibrahim)

For they have believed in His existence and His power, and that He has absolute will by which He keeps them firm, whatever the magnitude of the events. The believer knows with certainty that the Truth, glorified is He, has said and spoken truly:

﴿Verily, in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest.﴾ (28) (al-Ra'd)

And as long as the believer's heart is made firm by faith and by the firm word, he is not exposed to the deviation (zaygh)² of the heart, and he does not waver from the truth.

Steadfastness differs in people's customs according to the one who makes firm. When a pillar in the wall of a house becomes loose, the owner of the house brings the engineer who builds supports to make this pillar firm, and people admire the abilities of this engineer, and speak of the abilities of this engineer in making firm the pillars that were nearly collapsing. This is what is spoken of in the custom of men, so what of what the Creator of men can do?

His true saying:

﴿Allah keeps firm those who believe...﴾ (27) (Ibrahim)

brings you back to the One who makes firm, whose firming will never suffer the slightest defect. The word "tathbit" has shown us that man is a son of changing circumstances, and things may happen to him that do not correspond to what he wants in life, therefore the believer must not weaken, for he has a Lord whom eyes cannot perceive, and He perceives the eyes.

And He, glorified is He, keeps firm those who believe:

﴿with the firm word in the life of this world...﴾ (27) (Ibrahim)

The word is firm because it is of the Truth which does not change, and this word is addressed to the believers who are confronted by wicked people who have chosen to be on other than the method of Allah.

This word makes clear to the believers the necessity that they calm down, that they always place themselves in the company of Allah, and that they know that if the wrongdoer knew what Allah has prepared for the wronged of reward and good recompense, he would begrudge his wrongdoing to the wronged and would say: "And why should I make Allah my opponent?"

Those who were persecuted in their religion, whom the unbelievers tortured, were not turned away from the religion. Just as the unbelievers were harsh upon them with beating and torture, whenever they remembered the tenderness of the Truth they bore what the disbelievers made them taste of torment.

The good recompense may be in this world, in which the believer is made firm by the will of Allah, and it is the daughter of changing circumstances and the daughter of causes. You obtain anything in this world by toiling to get it, striving to learn, finding a job or profession, then marrying to form a family and serving others, and others serve you, and you pursue all your causes through others: you eat what your wife cooks, or your mother, or the one you employ to do this work for you.

In short, whenever you rise, you rise by the effect of some effort. Every pleasure you obtain is the result of serious effort on your part, and you always try to minimize effort and causes in order to increase your enjoyment.

So what of the Hereafter, in which there is no obligation and no causes, and everything in it has been prepared in advance by the Exalted Truth for man: a reward if he believes, and a punishment if he disbelieves and disobeys. And if you are a believer, Allah, glorified is He, will recompense you with a Garden whose breadth is the heavens and the earth, in which is all that the souls desire.

If Allah, glorified is He, keeps firm those who believe in this world with the true firm word, then His keeping them firm in the Hereafter is a life without causes.

We find that He, glorified is He, did not say here: "the Hereafter life," but said:

﴿in the life of this world and in the Hereafter...﴾ (27) (Ibrahim)

For the ambitious rises in life are proportionate to the effort exerted in them, but the matter in the Hereafter differs entirely, for the Truth, glorified is He, is the One who recompenses according to the extent of His absolute will, and He keeps them firm from the questioning in the grave to the end when they meet the reward for the good they did in the way of Allah.

Since Allah, glorified is He, has mentioned here steadfastness in this world and the Hereafter, there must be a counterpart, and He says:

﴿And Allah leads astray the wrongdoers, and Allah does what He wills.﴾ (27) (Ibrahim)

Allah, glorified is He, leads astray the wrongdoer because he chose to do wrong. He, glorified is He, has given man the right of choice, so whoever chooses to do wrong must have a punishment. And since He, glorified is He, created creation and made the universe subservient to them, and gave both believer and disbeliever of the gift of lordship, if the disbeliever chooses his disbelief, he will not carry out the obligations of divinity which Allah sent down as a method for guiding people.

The disbeliever only wrongs himself, for as long as he has become accustomed to disbelief, the Truth seals his heart so that disbelief does not leave the heart and faith does not enter it, and He, Lord of the worlds, does what He wills.

And since Allah, glorified is He, gives every person what he wants, and as long as the disbeliever asks to be a disbeliever, He extends for him the causes of disbelief so that afterwards He may seize him by them, just as Allah extends to the believers all the causes of faith, in confirmation of His true saying:

﴿To these and to those We extend from the gift of your Lord, and the gift of your Lord is not restricted.﴾ (20) (al-Isra')

Thus is the absoluteness of the power of the Truth, glorified is He, as He does what He wills, for there is no god besides Him.

The Truth, glorified is He, has honoured us with worship of Him alone, for we have all seen and witnessed the effect of human slavery to man, when the master takes the best of the slave, and humanity has tasted much of its calamities. But servitude to Allah differs entirely, for the slave takes the best of the master, and the master lavishes his kindness upon his servants.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 14, verse 28:

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says afterwards:

﴿Have you not seen those who exchanged the favour of Allah for ingratitude and caused their people to alight in the abode of ruin?(1) 28﴾

When the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿Have you not seen... 28﴾ (Ibrahim).

This means that the One who informs us, who is the Truth, when He tells us something, is more truthful than that our eyes should see it.

The verse points to a process of exchange: first an acknowledgement of the blessing, then the denial of it.

There was something we had set aside, and we brought in a substitute for it. The Truth, glorified is He, is the One who said:

﴿Would you exchange what is lower for what is better? ...61﴾ (al-Baqarah).

Allah, glorified and exalted is He, has given you the blessing and did not ask you to undertake any obligation of faith before reaching maturity. Thus we find that the blessing is the origin, and obligation comes after that. It was obligatory that the servant should not disobey the One who has bestowed upon him all blessings, and that he should turn to obligation with love, so that he does not turn the blessing of Allah into ingratitude.

Or: the intended ones are the people of Quraysh, upon whom Allah bestowed good and made the Sacred Precinct a place of safety:

﴿Did We not establish for them a safe sanctuary, to which the fruits of every thing are brought as provision from Us? But most of them do not know. 57﴾ (al-Qasas).

Likewise He blessed them by making the Prophet of Islam, the seal of religions, from among them, the Prophet before whom the world and the whole world will submit in every age and place. Why then would they exchange that blessing for ingratitude?

Was that blessing alone not sufficient to be met with deep gratitude and good worship? This is the Prophet concerning whose message the Truth, glorified is He, said:

﴿And indeed it is a reminder for you and your people, and you will be questioned. 44﴾ (al-Zukhruf).

And He, glorified is He, said concerning His blessings upon them:

﴿For the accustomed security of the Quraysh, their security in the caravan of winter and summer, let them worship the Lord of this House, who has fed them against hunger and made them secure from fear. 1-4﴾ (Quraysh).

How then do they exchange the favour of Allah for ingratitude? And how do they mistreat the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and his companions, until the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: (O Allah, make their years like the years of Yusuf)(4).

He went out to fight them at Badr, and they were those who brought this upon themselves as a result of their exchanging the favour of Allah for ingratitude. Why did they accept the gifts of the Truth of goodness and blessings, yet reject His method?

Had they been a people sincere with themselves, and sincere with what they believe, they would have asked the idols to give them, or they would have refused to take the good of the Giver, since they rejected His method, while He, glorified is He, had bestowed upon them the means of material sustenance, and added to that His method, which sustains the spirit.

When we read the saying of the Truth, glorified is He:

﴿And caused their people to alight in the abode of ruin 28﴾ (Ibrahim).

We understand that ihlal (causing to alight) is the bringing of one thing into the place of another. We know that the adverb (zarf) divides into two kinds: adverb of place and adverb of time. If you cause one event to alight in place of another event, this pertains to the adverb of time, and when you place one thing in the place of another thing, this matter pertains to the adverb of place.

Here the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿And caused their people to alight in the abode of ruin 28﴾ (Ibrahim).

This means an adverb of place. And one might say: how do they take their families and their people and cause them to alight in an abode of ruin?

We say: this happened as a result of their deceiving and misleading them, and these families did not use their minds, and did not notice that their leaders and those in authority among them were following bad conduct and they should not imitate them. So they dragged them into trials one after another, and the trials pile up (rayn) upon the hearts.

For this reason, the Truth, glorified is He, wanted the Ummah of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, to have within it immunities against trials, so that the self-reproaching soul (nafs al-lawwamah) urges the believer; so he increases good deeds to nullify bad deeds, and if the self-reproaching soul turns into a soul that commands evil (nafs ammarah bi-l-su'), it finds in the Muslim society one who restrains it.

Thereby the Ummah of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, becomes fortified against the trials that take away faith.

The Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿You are the best nation brought forth for mankind, enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong... 110﴾ (Al 'Imran).

The Truth, glorified is He, reminds us that the Messenger will be a witness over us, and we will be witnesses over the people. Thus the Truth, glorified is He, ensured that every one of the Ummah of Muhammad would know a portion of knowledge, to be an extension of the message of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

Just as the Messenger bore witness that he had conveyed the message, it will be incumbent upon every individual of the Ummah of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, to bear witness that he has conveyed what he knew of the message of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

Each of us knows how the first heedlessness occurred: when heedlessness became exemplary, desires overwhelmed them and they committed misdeeds. When the self became heedless it committed disobedience; when people saw someone committing disobedience, they imitated him.

Thus whoever fell into heedlessness bore his own burden and the burden of whoever followed him in the bad example, so he became misguided in himself, and then bore the burden of the one who misled him as well.

Thus the one who did this became the one who caused his people to alight in the abode of ruin.

Al-bawar means destruction. The great ones among these people, when they acted and behaved in opposition to the method, bequeathed destruction upon those who followed them.

In the countryside we describe land unfit for cultivation as barren land (al-ard al-bur), and it is likewise said (we have made the land barren) meaning we destroyed what was in it of crops.

When we read the saying of the Truth:

﴿And caused their people to alight in the abode of ruin 28﴾ (Ibrahim).

We find in the word (their people) something that suggests baseness in those who commit this shameful act, for whoever destroys his own people must be base, and must be a professional of deceit and trickery. The people are those who stand with them, and it would have been fitting to strike the hand of whoever harms them, or deceives them, or cheats them.

1 Al-bawar: destruction. Dar al-bawar: the abode of destruction [Lisan al-Arab, root b-w-r]. What is meant by it is Jahannam. Said by Ibn Zayd. [Mentioned by al-Qurtubi in his tafsir: 5/3703]. Evidence for this is the saying of Allah after it: ﴿Jahannam, they will burn in it, and wretched is the destination 29﴾ (Ibrahim)..
2 Afa'a Allah 'alayhi fay'an: He granted him spoils of war through victory or without war. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/92]..
3 Juba al-kharaj wa-l-ma': he collected it. Allah's saying: ﴿to which the fruits of every thing are brought 57﴾ (al-Qasas) means that abundant fruits and good things are gathered to the Sacred Precinct of Makkah and driven to it. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/117]..
4 From Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, when he raised his head from the last rak'ah would say: (O Allah, tighten Your grip upon Mudar, O Allah, make it years like the years of Yusuf..) The hadith. Recorded by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (1006) and Ahmad in his Musnad (2/470, 502, 521)..
5 Al-rayn: the rust that rises on a sword and takes away its polish, and it is used metaphorically for the veil that covers the heart because of sins; ran al-sada 'alayhi: it prevailed over it and covered it entirely. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/282]..
6 Bur al-ard: that part of the land which has become barren and has not been made productive with crops. Al-Zajjaj said: al-ba'ir in language is the corrupt thing that has no good in it. He said: and likewise a barren land left unplanted is called ba'ira. [Lisan al-Arab, root b-w-r]..

Al-Sha'rawi, Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66), on surah 14, verse 29:

Almighty Allah explains this abode of perdition, saying:

﴿Hell, which they will enter, and wretched is the destination.﴾ (29)

If we measure Hell by places of rest, we will find no one who wishes Hell to be his dwelling, because a person loves to settle in a place where he finds comfort; and if he finds no comfort in a place, he leaves it.

Hell, which they will enter, will not be a dwelling in which they find the least comfort, because punishment is permanent therein. For this reason Almighty Allah describes it as:

﴿Wretched is the destination﴾ (29) (Ibrahim).

It is as though they are held with hooks (2), so they cannot escape from it. And it says:

﴿Is there any more?﴾ (30) (Qaf).

It is as though they have fallen in love with the Fire, and the Fire has fallen in love with them. Had they the power to flee from it, they would have fled, but they are bound to it and it is bound to them. It is a wretched destination, because no one will leave it except as Allah wills.

(1) Asla al-nar: he made him enter it and lodged him therein. Sallayt al-nar means: I suffered its heat. Sala al-lahm: he roasted the meat. Al-sila': roasted meat, because it is roasted by fire. [Lisan al-Arab, root ṣ-l-y]

(2) Al-kalalib (sing. kullab): an iron piece with a bent head, like a hook. [Lisan al-Arab, root k-l-b]

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 14, verse 30:

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And they set up rivals to Allah, to lead [others] astray from His way. Say: "Enjoy yourselves, for your destination is the Fire."﴾ [14:30]

The *nidd* (rival) is: the like and the equal. They have taken partners for Allah; yet no partner they have taken has told them of the blessings with which He has showered them, nor has any sent down to them a method (*manhaj*). These partners were idols, or trees, or the sun, or the moon, or the stars, and none of these beings has said: "What blessings have I bestowed, that they should worship me?"

We know that worship (*ʿibadah*) requires a command and a prohibition, yet none of these partners sent down a method for those who worship them to follow, nor is there any reward for worship or punishment for not worshipping.

Therefore we find that such people turned to worshipping these partners because they did not bring a method to which they could commit themselves.

For this reason we find the impostors who claim that they have seen the Prophet (ﷺ), and who behave toward those who believe them among their followers as though they were beings superior to the Prophet (ﷺ) – we seek refuge in Allah from them.

What is strange is that we find some of the cultured people following these impostors, while simple folk may keep away from them. This is because the innate nature (*nafs al-fitriyyah*) loves to live upon the natural disposition of faith; but as for the one who comes to lighten the rulings of religion, some of those who seek release from the method are inclined to him.

Thus these followers make the one who lightens the method for them a rival to Allah – we seek refuge in Allah – and by this they go astray from faith.

The Truth, glory be to Him, says here:

﴿And they set up rivals to Allah, to lead [others] astray from His way...﴾ [14:30]

That is: to lead others astray from the way of Allah.

There is another reading (1) of the same verse (*liyaḍillū ʿan sabīlihi*, with the *yāʾ* opened), and when you hear an event that exists so that another event may come as its result, you use the *lām* of causation (*lām al-taʿlīl*), as when you say "the student studies so that he may pass" – here you have not brought an act and its opposite. Did they then lead themselves astray?

No, rather they imagined that they were upon guidance and uprightness. This is called the *lām al-ʿāqibah* (the *lām* of consequence), and it means that after the act there may occur another act that was expected. This too is called the *lām taʿlīliyyah*.

But an act may follow an act that its doer did not intend, as Pharaoh did when he picked up Moses, peace be upon him, from the water so that he might become his son; but Allah, glory be to Him, willed that he become an enemy to him.

At the time Pharaoh picked up Moses, Pharaoh did not wish that Moses should grow up to become his enemy; rather it was the will of Allah that willed it, in order to refute the one who thought himself able to control events – beginning with his claim of divinity, passing through the slaughter of the male children, and then his picking up of Moses to be a comfort of the eye for him, so that Moses grew up to become his enemy!!

The Truth, glory be to Him, continues:

﴿Say: "Enjoy yourselves, for your destination is the Fire."﴾ [14:30]

This is a command from Allah to Muhammad to say to them: "Enjoy yourselves." This is a command from Allah, and worship is a command from Allah. Would they, by enjoying themselves, have obeyed Allah?

Here we say: this is a command of mockery (*amr tahakkumī*), for the Truth, glory be to Him, said afterwards:

﴿For your destination is the Fire.﴾ [14:30]

Accordingly, we find that a command is either intended to bring about the carrying out of a request, or it is intended to turn away from the request by way of mockery.

We find in the saying of Imam ʿAli – may Allah ennoble his face – a statement that explains this to us: "There is no evil in an evil after which is Paradise, and no good in a good after which is the Fire."

So whoever says that the obligations are difficult should remember that after them is Paradise, and whoever sees sins and disbelief as a light matter should know that his destination after that is the Fire. Do not separate the preliminaries from their causes, nor the cause from its effect, nor the premise from its outcomes.

A father who sees his son pursuing study night and day to build his future may pity him, take the book from his hand, and order him to rest lest he fall ill and become like one cut off (*munbatt*) – neither a land traversed nor a mount left behind (2) – but the son desires to continue the effort to reach an honourable station.

Here we find that both the father and the son have looked at the good from different angles; therefore the difference in viewing events may be a means of meeting in the good within events.

And when they hear the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him:

﴿Say: "Enjoy yourselves, for your destination is the Fire."﴾ [14:30]

they may consider the events slow, and one of them says: "Until this destination comes, we will surely find a solution to it."

We say: let every person remember that a matter hanging on no fixed appointment may come suddenly. As for one who lives in disobedience until the age of ninety, does he think he will escape the Fire?

He is deluded, deceiving himself, for Allah's concealment of the appointed time of death is the most forceful declaration about it. And as long as the destination is the Fire, there is no enjoyment in that life.

(1) This is the reading of Ibn Kathir and Abu ʿAmr. al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir (5/3703): "As for the one who opens (the *yāʾ*), it is on the meaning that they themselves go astray from the way of Allah necessarily, i.e., their consequence is to misguidance and going astray; this is the *lām al-ʿāqibah*."

(2) *al-Inbitat*: cutting off. A man who is *munbatt* is one cut off from his journey. [Lisan al-ʿArab, root b-t-t]. *al-Zahr*: the camels that are loaded and ridden. [Lisan al-ʿArab, root z-h-r].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 14, verse 31:

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says:

﴿Say to My servants who have believed: establish the prayer and spend from what We have provided them, secretly and openly, before there comes a Day in which there is no trading and no friendship.﴾ (31)

The "say" is from Allah to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Does this mean that the servants who hear this command will rise to prayer? Some of them have heard it and did not rise to prayer.

So, whoever obeys the command is the one who has fulfilled the condition of faith. We must look at the context of the word "My servants" ('ibadi): the servants of Allah are those who have believed, and when they believe they will express this faith through obedience. Thus we understand the meanings of the words so that their meanings are upheld in their usages.

All of Allah's creation are His servants ('abid), because there are matters that Allah willed in the manner of their creation, over which they have no power to oppose. He has subdued them in some things and given them choice in other things.

For this reason I always say to those who rebel against faith in Allah: you have become accustomed to rebelling against Allah, and not one of your natures refuses to reject rebellion. If you are truthful with yourselves, you should rebel against breathing, which is an involuntary matter, or rebel—if you are able—against sickness and the appointed time of death, and you will never be able to do that.

But they have become accustomed to rebelling against what they can choose. They forget that Allah wants them to adhere to His method. If the believer chooses to follow the method of Allah, he becomes one of the "servants of Allah" ('ibad Allah); and if he does not submit to the method in what is left to his choice, he is among the servants (ʿabīd) subdued to follow the compulsory commands of Allah only.

When you survey the word "servants" ('ibad) and the word "servants" ('abid) in the Qur'an, you will find the words of the Truthful, glorified is He:

﴿And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth in humility, and when the ignorant address them, they say, "Peace."﴾ (63) (al-Furqan).

Here the attributes of the servants who chose to follow the method of Allah are multiplied, and you will find the word "servants" ('abid) attached to those who rebel against the method of Allah. You will not find them described as "servants" ('ibad) except in one verse, when the Truthful, may He be exalted, addresses those who misled people, and says to them:

﴿Did you mislead these My servants, or did they themselves stray from the way?﴾ (17) (al-Furqan).

We note that the time of this address is the Last Day, when no one has any intercessor with Allah, and when the Truthful, glorified is He, removes all right of choice from the created beings who were given choice.

Thus no one can dispute that the word "servants" ('ibad) is used to describe those who chose to worship Allah and adhere to His method in the worldly life, since they have handed over the reins of their choice to Allah and obeyed Him in His commands and prohibitions.

We note that the saying of the Truthful, glorified is He:

﴿Say to My servants who have believed: establish the prayer and spend from what We have provided them, secretly and openly..﴾ (31) (Ibrahim).

is a command issued by the Truthful, glorified is He, to His Messenger (ﷺ), and that the believers are awaiting this command in order to carry it out immediately, since the believer loves to carry out every command that comes to him from Allah.

And since you, O Muhammad, have conveyed this command to them, they will carry it out at once. The word "yuqimu" (establish) has come with the jussive particle lam of command omitted, to emphasize that they will hasten (1) to carry out the command upon hearing it.

Commonly in the bulk of Qur'anic verses (2), the establishment of prayer and the giving of zakat come in succession with one another, because establishing the prayer requires movement, requires energy and takes fuel, and fuel requires movement and takes time; and zakat means that you bring forth a portion of the fruit of time, and a portion of the effect of movement in the period.

And we find those who are lazy about prayer saying: "Work takes all the time, and one of us tries to gather the prayers until the end of the day and performs them all as make-up (qada')." They do not notice that every obligation, when performed at its appointed time, will not take the amount of time they imagine to be large.

The apparent matter is that prayer reduces the fruit of work, but the truth is that it gives a charge and energy that stimulates the soul to further perfection of work. How can the one who prays come to work with a contented soul? Because by prayer he has stood in the presence of the One who created him, provided for him, and sustains him.

For this reason he comes out of it calm, reassured, attentive and content, and for this reason the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to say: "Give us rest by it, O Bilal" (3).

Prayer in each obligatory form will not take more than a quarter of an hour including ablution, and if you compare the time of all the prayers to the time of work, you will find that it takes a small proportion and gives back more than it took.

Likewise zakat may take from you some of the fruit of time to give it to the one who is unable, but it grants you a social security beyond what you imagine.

For this reason you find prayer linked with zakat in the verses of the Qur'an, one with the other. The establishment of prayer is the sum of all values, and the giving of zakat is the sum of the establishment of all bodily movements.

Prayer addresses one thing, and zakat addresses another thing; both of them reform the components of the human reality: the spirit and its constituents, and the body and its constituents.

For this reason he (ﷺ) said: "The coolness of my eyes has been made to be in prayer" (4).

When you look at prayer and zakat, you find the interests of life gathered and branching out from them, because the Messenger (ﷺ) gathered the interests of life in the five pillars of religion, which are: the testimony that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, the establishment of prayer, the giving of zakat, the fasting of Ramadan, and the pilgrimage to the House for whoever is able to make his way to it (5).

We have already known how prayer took up all these pillars together: in it is the testimony that there is no god but Allah; in it is sacrifice and purification by part of the time; in it is abstention from everything you are bound by while you are fasting; and you turn during it toward the qibla of the Sacred House of Allah.

Thus we see how the movement of life and the values that reform it are linked with prayer and zakat.

In this noble verse Allah commands us to spend secretly and openly. Thus the Truthful makes spending general in two opposite matters: spending secretly, so that a person does not fall prey to showing off, and spending openly, so that he gives others among the able an excellent example, and so that you prevent others from speaking about you in a tone containing envy and jealousy at the good that Allah has bestowed upon you.

For this reason I say: make voluntary charity secret, and make it as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Let not your left hand know what your right hand has given" (6).

And make zakat open, so that people know that you are paying what is due to you of Allah's rights, and so that it becomes for them a practical example and a practical admonition. Make of the pillars of Islam a behavioural admonition, for we see some villages and cities from which no one performs the pilgrimage, because the able among them have already performed the obligation of Hajj.

We find that the able person who builds a mosque gives an example to the other able person to build another mosque; and as soon as Ramadan comes, the able fast, and they give an example to their children; and humiliation before others is prevented. Thus we declare all the obligations of Islam clearly before all societies.

The Truthful, glorified is He, says:

﴿Say to My servants who have believed: establish the prayer and spend from what We have provided them, secretly and openly, before there comes a Day in which there is no trading and no friendship.﴾ (31) (Ibrahim).

From here we know that there are actions that you may postpone, except the aims in which there are no compensations; so you must seize the opportunity and carry them out immediately, since the Last Day will have no buying or selling, and no one will be able to give alms or pray there; there is no friendship or intercession that will suffice you for what you should have done in the worldly life.

Intercession alone is what the Most Merciful has permitted (7), and therefore the command here comes with haste to perform prayer, give zakat, and spend secretly and openly before the day comes in which there is no trading and no friendship.

Trading, as we know, is an exchange of opposites: there is one who pays the price, and there is one who takes the goods. Khilal is mukhallah, i.e., the faithful friend whom you are bound to and who is bound to you.

Poetry clarifies the meaning of the word "khalil" (friend) when it says:

When we met, longing brought its effort near,
two friends who melted with anguish and reproach.
As if one friend in the midst of his friend's embrace
slipped in during the embrace and vanished.

This shows that mukhallah means that each of the two penetrates the other.

In the Hereafter you will not be able to buy a paradise or ransom yourself from the Fire, and there is no mukhallah there by which a friend overflows upon you from his good deeds.

The Truthful, glorified is He, is the One who says:

﴿The intimate friends on that day will be enemies to one another, except the righteous.﴾ (67) (al-Zukhruf).

Some superficial people wish to object against the Qur'an that it affirmed friendship and negated it, for He says:

﴿There is no trading in it and no friendship.﴾ (Ibrahim).

And He says:

﴿And no friendship.. (254)﴾ (al-Baqarah).

Then He affirmed friendship for the righteous, those among whom neither one adorns sin for the other.

These superficial people do not know how to reflect on the Qur'an properly; the friendship that is negated, or the khilal that is negated, in the verses is the khilal that incites to sins, and these are the evil khilal.

We know that trading in the worldly life is the exchange of a commodity for a price; but mukhallah involves generosity from the one who offers it, and this is an apparent matter, because in its inner reality there is an exchange. If someone does you a favour, this requires that you return the favour to him; whereas pure generosity is that which occurs without a prior or subsequent [obligation].

(1) Khilal: either the plural of khullah or the verbal noun of khalla. The meaning: the Day of Resurrection does not save from His punishment anything; nothing is bought there with wealth by which the disbeliever ransoms himself, nor does friendship benefit him, for no friend suffices in place of a friend. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/208].
(2) Sada'tu ila al-shay': I inclined to it. [Lisan al-Arab, root ṣ-d-ʿ]. (Note: this footnote numbering follows the source's own notes.)
(3) This came in more than 27 verses of the Qur'an. [Mu'jam al-Mufahras li-Alfaz al-Qur'an].

Having shown us the people of happiness and the people of misery, and having struck the parable of the good word and the parable of the evil word, God, glory be to Him, now brings what stirs joy in the heart of the believer, because he believes in God, who made all those blessings, and He mentions blessings that no one shares with Him at all. So He says:

﴿God is He who created the heavens and the earth, and sent down water from the sky, and brought forth thereby fruits as provision for you, and subjected to you the ships (al-fulk) to run upon the sea by His command, and subjected to you the rivers.﴾ [32]

As we know, the heavens and the earth are the two vessels of life for all of us. God, may He be exalted, has said:

﴿Certainly the creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind...﴾ [40:57]

If God is the One who created the heavens and the earth, then this is a general indication for us, because He did not mention here what He mentioned in other places of the Noble Qur'an, that they are without pillars ('amad) and that there are no fissures in them, nor did He mention here that He placed in the earth firm mountains so that the earth would not shake with us, nor did He mention how He measured in the earth its sustenance, but He is content here with a glimpse of the creation of the heavens and the earth.

When God, may He be exalted, speaks here about the creation of the heavens and the earth, He brings a matter that no one has claimed, despite the abundance of claimants among the atheists. This is so that the proof against the opponent may be more binding, and thereby He reveals to them the reality of their disbelief, and makes them see that they disbelieved as a result of stubborn enmity (ladad) not subject to logic, which is disbelief without reasons.

When God issues a judgment for which there is no opponent or contender, this means that the judgment has been acknowledged for Him, glory be to Him. No one among the disbelievers has dared to oppose what God said; it is as if the disbeliever turns the matter over in his head and knows that no one has claimed for himself the creation of the heavens and the earth, and he finds no escape from submitting to the fact that God is the One who created the heavens and the earth.

The saying of God, may He be exalted, here:

﴿And God is He who created the heavens and the earth...﴾ [14:32]

clarifies for us that the word (Allah) here, because it is the locus of difficulty in the obligation (taklif), for the obligation stands before desires, and you may be angry at the obligation, but it protects you from one another and secures for you safety and a good life.

God, may He be exalted, did not use the word (Rabb) here, because it is the locus of the giving that He willed for mankind, believer and disbeliever alike.

The word (Allah) means the One worshipped who sends down commands and prohibitions, and it means that there are hardships; for this reason He mentioned to them that He created the heavens and the earth and sent down water from the sky.

When we hear the word (al-sama') we understand it to be the sky opposite the earth, but verification confirms that the sky is everything that is above you and shades you.

Rain, as we know, descends only from the clouds and the cumulus. God, may He be exalted, is the One who says:

﴿Do you not see that God drives the clouds, then joins them together, then makes them into a heap, and you see the rain coming out from their midst...﴾ [24:43]

We have come to know through experimental science that the airplane, for example, flies above the clouds, and accordingly the rain does not descend from the sky; rather it descends from what is above us of vapor and clouds.

Or: when you attribute descent to the sky, this clarifies for us that all our affairs come from above. For this reason we find iron, which the mountains embrace and which matures within them, of which God, may He be exalted, says:

﴿And We sent down iron, wherein is great might and benefits for mankind...﴾ [57:25]

Thus we find that either it descended as elements with the rain, or because the command of its formation descended from the sky.

And here, in the verse about which we are reflecting, God, may He be exalted, speaks of the creation of the heavens and the earth and how He sent down water from the sky:

﴿and brought forth thereby fruits as provision for you...﴾ [14:32]

The fruits (al-thamarat) are the produce of what the earth gives of plants, some of which you may eat and some of which you may not eat. For example, we eat grapes, but we do not eat the branches of the grapevine; likewise we eat oranges, but we do not eat the leaves and branches of the orange tree.

[1] Al-fulk: the ship, for the masculine and feminine, the singular and plural. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/89].

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on Surah Ibrahim (14), verse 33 (verse 32 in the text):

He, glorified be He, continues:

﴿And He has subjected for you the ships to run upon the sea by His command.﴾ (Ibrahim)

Taskhir (subjugation) means overpowering a thing so that it serves another thing. The subjugation of ships may raise a question in the mind: how does God subject the ship, when it is man who builds it?

But why does the one who asks not ask himself: from where do we obtain the timber from which we make the planks from which we build the ship? Then, who made water fluid, so that the ship floats upon it? And who set the winds in motion so that they push the ship?

All of that is from the marvellous creation of God, glorified be He.

The word (al-fulk) comes sometimes meaning a single thing, and sometimes meaning many things; it may be either singular or plural.

The example is the saying of the Truth, glorified be He:

﴿And the ships that run upon the sea with that which benefits people.﴾ (al-Baqarah)

Likewise He said in the story of Noah, peace be upon him:

﴿And construct the ship under Our eyes.﴾ (Hud)

Some scholars say: if the feminine pronoun refers back to it, it is plural; and if it refers back with the masculine, it is singular.

But I say: this view is not dominant, for He, glorified be He, said of Noah's ship, which is singular:

﴿Running under Our eyes.﴾ (al-Qamar)

He did not say (yajri bi-a'yunina), and thus the feminine form is not evidence of plurality.

He, glorified be He, continues:

﴿And He has subjected for you the rivers.﴾ (Ibrahim)

We naturally understand that the river has fresh water, while the sea's water is salty.

He, glorified be He, has subjected everything to us by His command. It is He who created the river with fresh water and made for it a depth that in some times permits the passage of ships, and at other times the depth does not permit this.

He made the sea deep-bottomed so that ships may glide through it. All of this is subjected by His command, and He, glorified be He, is the One who said:

﴿If He wills, He calms the wind so that they remain still upon its back.﴾ (al-Shura)

That is: He, glorified be He, may will that the winds stand still, so that the ships are becalmed in the seas and rivers.

Among the wonders of the Qur'an's announcements is that the Truth, glorified be He, when He spoke of the wind that drives the ship and the vessels, the formalists and superficial people said: "We no longer drive ships by the wind, but by energy."

We say: let us read His saying, the Truth:

﴿And do not dispute, lest you lose courage and your strength depart.﴾ (al-Anfal)

And (rihukum, your wind) means: your strength and your power. So the intended "wind" is absolute strength, whether it comes from air, from steam, or from water.

This verse, about which we are reflecting, was revealed after God, glorified be He, informed us of the story of the happy believers and the wretched disbelievers. That verse was thus a tribute to the believers who appreciated this blessing of God, so that when they knew of it they believed in Him, glorified be He.

This verse honoured them for the purity of their innate nature, which had not been clouded, and it honoured the intellect that reflected upon the universe and contemplated it with a gaze of consideration and reflection, to deduce from the phenomena of the universe that there is a Creator God, all-wise.

In the verse there is also a rebuke to the disbeliever who received these blessings, yet had not heard from anyone that it was created for him; he did not create it for himself; and yet he is arrogant, obstinate, and disbelieves in the Lord of these blessings.

The first of those blessings is the creation of the heavens and the earth; then, if you look at the remaining blessings, you will find that they came after the creation of the heavens and the earth; and some of those blessings are connected to the sky, such as the clouds, and some are connected to the earth, such as the fruits that it brings forth.

Thus, there is stylistic coherence between the first blessing and the second blessing.

Then He said after that:

﴿And He has subjected for you the ships to run upon the sea by His command.﴾ (Ibrahim)

What is the connection that makes this command come after these two commands? Because the ship's path is the seas and its course is in the water.

The Truth, glorified be He, has said that He created the heavens and the earth. The sense of "earth" applies to dry land as well as to water, and it is remarkable that water on the surface of the globe equals three times the dry land; the area of water is thus wider than the area of land on the earth.

Since the Truth, glorified be He, has said that He brought forth from the earth fruits that are our provision, there must be some relationship between that and this; so if the seas take three-quarters of the surface of the earth, then there must be something in them for man.

The Truth, glorified be He, has explained this in other verses, and made clear that He subjected the sea so that we may eat from it fresh meat, and that is the sustenance of life, and we extract from it ornaments we wear, and that is the luxury of life.

And we see ships ploughing through it (mawakhir) so that we may seek of His bounty.

Thus there are other goods beyond fish and ornaments, but they came in summary, not in detail. Perhaps the people, at the time of the Qur'an's revelation, were not able to understand and know all the goods that are in the seas, and scientific research still uncovers for us more of the goods of the seas.

When we now contemplate the goods of the seas, we marvel at the beauty of the creatures in them.

So His saying:

﴿That you may seek of His bounty.﴾ (al-Isra')

is a general statement that summarises the existence of other things besides fish and besides adornment such as pearls and coral and other things; and when we see the creatures of the ocean depths, we marvel at that creation more than we marvel at the creation on dry land, and at the creation of what is in the sky.

Thus His saying, the Truth:

﴿That you may seek of His bounty.﴾ (al-Isra')

is one of the verses of summary which the cosmic signs detail; for some Qur'anic verses are explained by the cosmic signs. For if the Truth, glorified be He, had explained every detail, people at the time of the Qur'an's revelation would not have believed it.

By way of example, when He spoke of means of transport, He said:

﴿And horses and mules and donkeys, for you to ride and as adornment; and He creates what you do not know.﴾ (al-Nahl)

And His saying, exalted be He:

﴿And He creates what you do not know.﴾ (al-Nahl)

includes everything we humans have invented of means of transport, even transport by buttons such as the fax and other things.

When He, glorified be He, speaks of the seas, He is clarifying for us what completes the discussion of the earth:

﴿And He has subjected for you the ships to run upon the sea by His command.﴾

(Ibrahim)

Had people been perceptive, they would have called ships "the camels of the sea," since they called the camel "the ship of the desert"; but they took the unknown by the known they possess.

Beware lest you say: "I am the one who made the sail, and I am the one who built the boat from planks," for you made all of that by the powers God created in you, and by the reason God bestowed upon you, and by the material God bestowed upon you; all of them are things that came by the command of God.

Here He, glorified be He, says:

﴿And He has subjected for you the rivers.﴾ (Ibrahim)

The river's water is usually fresh so as to irrigate the trees that produce fruit, and trees generally need fresh water.

Thus God willed that the water of the seas and oceans be a vast reservoir of water, occupying three-quarters of the surface of the globe, an immense area that offers the opportunity for evaporation, which by heat turns water into vapour that rises up and becomes cloud; then the cloud drops the water, after the salts have been removed during evaporation and it has become fresh water, from which the trees that need it are irrigated, and they produce for us the fruits we need; and it is as though the salts found in sea water are for preserving and protecting it from spoilage.

We know that most river water comes from rain, and thus is the cycle of water in the universe: water in the sea on which the sun shines to evaporate it, to become cloud, and afterwards falls as rain that nourishes the rivers and pours the excess back into the seas.

He, glorified be He, continues:

﴿And He has subjected for you the sun and the moon, both constant; and He has subjected for you the night and the day.﴾ (Ibrahim, 33)

The sun is a daytime sign, and the moon a nighttime sign; the water we drink is related to the sun, which evaporates it from the sea's water, and with which we also irrigate the land that produces fruit for us; as for the seas, the reckoning of all that happens in them is made according to the lunar calendar.

Did the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, know all that, being the unlettered Prophet?

Of course he did not know; rather, the Truth, glorified be He, revealed to him the Qur'an, which comprises all the realities of the universe.

The Truth's saying about the sun and moon, "constant" (da'ibayn), comes from da'b, and da'ub is the passing of a thing in a regular action; we say "so-and-so is diligent (da'ub) at studying," meaning he exerts orderly, regular effort to acquire his school subjects, and does not waste his time.

Likewise the sun and moon, for which the Truth, glorified be He, established a precise system.

For example, we reckon the day beginning with the night, then the day; and we divide the day into twenty-four hours; and therefore the Truth, glorified be He, said:

﴿The sun and the moon by reckoning.﴾ (al-Rahman)

And He also said:

﴿And the sun and the moon as a reckoning.﴾ (al-An'am)

That is: you, O human, will make the appearance and disappearance of either of them a reckoning.

He, the Truth, glorified be He, has made them with such precision of motion that it facilitates for us to reckon time by them, so there is no collision between them, and each of them has its own orbit and a movement calculated precisely, so they do not collide. They are, of course, not like the clocks we use, which need adjusting.

The more we advance in craftsmanship, the more we find that our inventions bring us closer to the depth of faith in the Supreme Creator.

In the same verse the Truth, glorified be He, says:

﴿And He has subjected for you the night and the day.﴾ (Ibrahim)

Since the sun is a daytime sign, and the moon a nighttime sign, and the day precedes the night in existence for us, the expected phrasing would have been: "He subjected for you the day and the night."

But the Truth, glorified be He, wanted to teach us that the moon, which is the nighttime sign and shines at night, and the night is created for rest, yet this rest is not the cause of man's existence on the earth; rather the cause is that man should move, settle the earth, toil and strive in it.

Therefore He placed the sun first at the beginning, and the moon draws its light from it; then He brought the report of the night and the report of the day; as though God has enveloped this verse with two lights.

The first light: from the sun. The second light: from the moon, so that man knows that his life is wrapped in a way that allows him movement on the earth; so do not suppose, O human, that the basis is sleep! God created sleep so that you rest, then you wake to toil.

We note that the word "subjection" (taskhir) comes for essential things, and comes for the subjected things too: the animal is subjected for us, and likewise plants, and the heavens with what is in them are subjected for us; as for night and day, they are two results of substances, namely the sun and the moon, and night and day are caused by two direct things, namely:

the sun and the moon.

Subjection, as we know, is the removal of choice. When the Truth, glorified be He, subjects a thing, know that it is regulated and no disorder can occur in it; but the being that is not subjected is the one in which disorder can occur, for it may walk the right path or it may err.

On the question of subjection and choice, philosophers have laboured in studying it, and philosophical schools, especially in Germany, arrived at two doctrines apparently in contradiction, but which lead to one goal, namely justifying atheism.

It would have been acceptable for one of them to justify atheism and the other to justify faith; but the philosophers of both doctrines chose to justify atheism.

The philosophers of one doctrine said: you say that the universe is run by a powerful, wise force, and that everything in it is regulated by calculated and precise actions.

But reality says: there are some anomalies we see in beings, such as the peculiarities in man: for example, there is one who is too short, and one who is too tall, and one who is born with one eye, and one who is born with a withered arm; and if the force that runs the universe were wise, such peculiarities would not have appeared.

We reply to the proponent of that theory, saying: and if it is not

(Fatir 12).

[al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/306].

Then He opened the field to other blessings that no one can count.

So, glorified is He, after that He says:

﴿And He gave you of all that you asked Him. And if you should count the favor of Allah, you could not enumerate them. Indeed, mankind is [generally] a wrongdoer and ungrateful.﴾ [14:34]

Yes, the Truth (al-Haqq), glorified is He, has given us of what we ask and before we ask, and He prepared the universe for us before we came into existence. So, glorified is He, He gave us before we asked; the blessing preceded the existence of Adam, peace be upon him, and the universe received Adam, having been prepared to receive him.

If you look at any one of us individually, you will find that Allah's blessings upon him preceded our knowing how to ask Him, and the example is the fetus in its mother's womb.

Here the Truth, glorified is He, said:

﴿And He gave you of all that you asked [of Him]...﴾ [14:34] (Ibrahim).

That is: He has given you what you ask for and what you do not ask for, whether you utter it or not, even by an inner speech or hidden thoughts, and that when you propose and request something, He gives it to you.

Some people may ask, out of a desire for challenge — and to Allah belongs the highest likeness — we find some humans upon whom Allah has bestowed abundant blessings, and one of them says: "Tell me, what do you request?"

This happened to me in a similar way while I was a guest of one whom Allah honoured with His generous giving, and we were on a desert journey in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. He said to me: "Ask for anything and, by Allah's permission, you will find it present." I thought to ask for something that could not possibly be found there, and I said: "I want a thread and a needle." His response was only: "Do you want it as a white strand or a red one?"

If this happens among humans, then what of Allah's power to give?

From the wisdom of Allah, glorified is He, that He said:

﴿And He gave you of all that you asked [of Him]...﴾ [14:34] (Ibrahim).

For behind every giving there is wisdom, and behind every withholding there is also wisdom. Withholding from Allah is itself a form of giving. The Truth, glorified is He, is far above being employed by you, just as the Truth, glorified is He, said:

﴿And mankind supplicates for evil as he supplicates for good...﴾ [17:11] (al-Isra').

And therefore He said:

﴿And He gave you of all that you asked [of Him]...﴾ [14:34] (Ibrahim).

That is: some of what you asked, for there are foolish requests that Allah does not answer for you, such as the saying of a woman whose son defies her: "Let him give me to drink of your fire." This woman — if Allah made her taste the fire of losing her son, what would she do?

So, from His greatness, glorified is He, that He gave us what is in accordance with wisdom and withheld from us what is not in accordance with His wisdom. Giving is a blessing, and withholding is also a blessing. If each of us looked at what appears to be deprivation, he would find in it many blessings.

He, glorified is He, says:

﴿I will show you My signs, so do not ask Me to hasten them.﴾ [21:37] (al-Anbiya').

Therefore let no one say: "I have supplicated my Lord and He has not responded to me," and man must remember the saying of the Truth, glorified is He:

﴿And mankind supplicates for evil as he supplicates for good, and mankind has always been hasty.﴾ [17:11] (al-Isra').

He, glorified is He, possesses the wisdom of giving and the wisdom of withholding. None of us can count the blessings of Allah. Counting — as we know — is the enumeration of the units of a collective or the parts of a whole. Those learned in logic — whom we call the mantiqa (logicians) — know that there is a "universal" (kulli), which is opposed by a "particular" (juz'i), and there is a "whole" (kull), which is opposed by a "part" (juz').

An example of the "universal" is the human being, since we are all composed of similar elements, and the individual members of mankind differ in their names. As for what is called a "whole" (kull), the example of it is the chair, which is composed of different materials such as wood, nails and glue, and we cannot apply the word "chair" to the wood alone, nor can we call the "nails" chairs.

From this we have understood that the reality of the universal is that its members are identical, though their names differ; but the reality of the whole is that its components are not alike and differ in their nature.

If you wish to count the universal, you pronounce the names of the individuals, as when you say: Muhammad, Ahmad and Ali; this is what is called 'add (counting). Thus we understand that 'add is the enumeration of the particulars of the universal, or the enumeration of the parts of the whole.

We know that they called counting "iḥṣā'" (enumeration), because in ancient times they counted things with pebbles (ḥaṣa), and the word iḥṣā' was applied to counting in general, by way of reference to the origin, and the number of the parts of the universal or the whole became known.

Man in ancient times — for example — would count up to the number "one hundred," and then count each hundred with a single pebble; when he had gathered ten pebbles he knew that the number had become a thousand. From here came the word iḥṣā'. In many matters of our advanced age we still name some things by old designations; for example, we measure the power of a car by horsepower.

When you consider the saying of the Truth, glorified is He:

﴿And if you should count the favor of Allah, you could not enumerate them.﴾ [14:34] (Ibrahim).

you will find many meanings. But those who seek to find faults in the Qur'an say: "This is an imprecise matter; since counting has taken place, how is enumeration not achieved?" These people forget that the intended meaning here is not counting itself, but the intention to count.

If the intention exists, there is still no capacity to comprehend Allah's blessings. From here we see no contradiction in the signs of Allah; rather, it is an integrated system. You do not undertake to count a matter unless it is probable that you are able to count it, and that is when it is within human capacity; but Allah's blessings are beyond human capacity.

An example of the intention to do an act can also be found in the saying of the Truth:

﴿O you who have believed, when you rise to prayer, wash your faces...﴾ [5:6] (al-Ma'idah).

We do not wash our faces at the moment we begin prayer, but we wash them and complete the steps of wudu' when the muezzin calls and we have the intention to pray. So the meaning here is: when you intend to rise to prayer, do such-and-such.

We know that mentioning a thing by its cause is as if it were the thing itself. Therefore it is said: if the adhan has been called in the mosque while you are leaving your home intending to pray, do not run to catch up with the imam and attain the prayer,(1) for you are in prayer from the moment you performed wudu' and left your house for prayer. Beware of making any movement that contradicts prayer; enter the mosque with tranquility and dignity to perform the prayer with the imam.(2)

When we reflect on the saying of the Truth:

﴿And if you should count the favor of Allah, you could not enumerate them.﴾ [14:34] (Ibrahim).

you will find that the custom in the language is to use "in" (in) for an uncertain matter, while for a certain matter we use "when" (idha), as in the saying of the Truth:

﴿When there has come the help of Allah and the victory﴾ [110:1] (al-Nasr).

Here the Truth, glorified is He, has used the style of doubt when He said:

﴿And if you should count the favor of Allah, you could not enumerate them.﴾ [14:34] (Ibrahim).

For the intelligent person knows in advance that he will be unable to enumerate the blessings of Allah. We all know that there is a science called "statistics" (al-ihsa'), which has specialized university departments.

Despite progress and the manufacture of computers, no one has been able to, or has undertaken to, enumerate Allah's blessings in the universe, for counting and enumeration require a universal that has members, or a whole that has parts.

If you look at any blessing of Allah, you may think it is one blessing, but if you analyse it you will find it to be multiple and varied blessings. Thus there is no contradiction in the saying of the Truth:

﴿And if you should count the favor of Allah, you could not enumerate them.﴾ [14:34] (Ibrahim).

If you take the blessing of water, you will find it to be many blessings, for it is composed of elements, each element of which is a blessing; and if you take the blessing of the earth, you will find in it many hidden blessings. Thus every blessing from Allah contains multiple blessings within it, and they cannot be counted.

When you contemplate the saying of the Truth, glorified is He:

﴿And if you should count the favor of Allah, you could not enumerate them.﴾ [14:34] (Ibrahim).

you find three elements: the Bestower (al-Mun'im), the blessing, which the Truth, glorified is He, has judged you will not be able to enumerate, and that His creatures have not ventured to undertake to count that blessing, for it cannot be counted because it is not liable to enumeration, and no intelligent person would accept to enumerate it.

The third element is the one upon whom the blessing is bestowed (al-mun'am 'alayh), who is the human being, who may be unable to enumerate the blessings of his superior among men upon him — how much more the blessings of Allah which cannot be counted, His perfections which are not limited, and His giving which never ends? And to Allah belongs the highest likeness, for He is far above any likeness.

Then comes the saying of the Truth, glorified is He:

﴿Indeed, mankind is [generally] a wrongdoer and ungrateful.﴾ [14:34] (Ibrahim).

Here in Surat Ibrahim we find the saying of the Truth clarifying man's wronging of himself and his ingratitude for the blessing, and in his ingratitude for blessings there is ingratitude toward the Bestower. He, glorified and exalted is He, says:

﴿Have you not seen those who exchanged the favor of Allah for ingratitude and caused their people to alight at the abode of destruction? [They will enter] Hell, which they will [burn in] — and wretched is the place of settlement.﴾ [14:28–29] (Ibrahim).

These are the ones who committed injustices concerning the belief in divine oneness and faith in Allah. Man is the one upon whom blessings are bestowed, and it would not be proper for him to see all these blessings and then reject them. It would be just to give the right to its owner; but some humans have exchanged the favor of Allah for ingratitude, and thus they have become those of whom it is said that each one of them is a wrongdoer in judgment and an ungrateful one, for denying the blessing and disowning the Creator's giving to the creature.

Wronging, as we know, is to transfer a right from its owner to someone other than its owner. If you do not believe in Allah, you have taken the right of God to existence; and if you believe in partners, you transfer thereby a right from Allah to another, and this is the greatest wrong.

Consider the saying of the Truth, glorified is He, in Surat al-Nahl:

﴿And He subjected to you the night and the day and the sun and the moon, and the stars are subjected by His command. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reason. And what He has created for you on the earth of varying colors. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who are mindful. And it is He who subjected the sea for you to eat from it tender meat and to extract from it ornaments which you wear; and you see the ships therein plowing [through it], and [He created them] that you may seek of His bounty and perhaps you will be grateful. And He placed on the earth firmly set mountains lest it shake with you, and rivers and roads, that you may be guided. And landmarks; and by the star they [mankind] are guided. Then is He who creates like one who does not create? Then will you not remember? And if you should count the favor of Allah, you could not enumerate them. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ [16:12–18] (al-Nahl).

Is there, then, any will or power that can enumerate the gifts of Allah which exceed counting and limit? In the preceding verses and others there is both miraculousness and incapacity, and since there is incapacity, His perfection is unending.

Indeed, some who object to the Qur'an say: "How does the Qur'an say once:

﴿And if you should count the favor of Allah, you could not enumerate them. Indeed, mankind is [generally] a wrongdoer and ungrateful.﴾ [14:34] (Ibrahim).

and then say in another verse:

﴿And if you should count the favor of Allah, you could not enumerate them. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ [16:18] (al-Nahl)?"

We respond to these: you have not looked at the context in which each verse came, and your insight has been blinded from knowing that the context of the verse — with which we are concerned in these reflections — mentions blessings and mentions denial and ingratitude for blessings, and this arises from man's great wronging of himself.

In the verse of Surat al-Nahl He mentioned blessings, and despite our wronging, His mercy encompassed us, and He did not withhold the blessings He has lavished upon us. It is as if He, glorified is He, clarifies for us: "Beware of being shy to ask Me for anything; and if you have wronged and disbelieved in some matters, your wrong is met by My forgiveness, and your ingratitude is met by My mercy." Thus there is no contradiction between the two verses; rather, each conclusion is suitable to its verse: in the first verse Allah treats us with His justice, and in the second verse Allah treats us with His grace.

We note that the Truth, glorified is He, has said here:

﴿Indeed, mankind is [generally] a wrongdoer and ungrateful.﴾ [14:34] (Ibrahim).

We know that there are people who have believed in Allah and His blessings and thank Allah for them; so how does the Truth, glorified is He, describe man as a wrongdoer and ungrateful?

We say: the word "man" (insan), when used without exception, tends toward loss and a life without method, and without turning to reflect upon the universe.

When the Truth, glorified is He, wanted to clarify this for us, He said:

﴿By time, indeed, mankind is in loss, except those who have believed and done righteous deeds and advised each other to truth and advised each other to patience.﴾ [103:1–3] (al-'Asr).

Therefore He, glorified is He, brought the exception after it.
