Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 14, verse 35:

Then He, glorified is He, says after that:

﴿And when Abraham said: "My Lord, make this city secure and keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols."﴾ (35)

When He, glorified is He, says "idhā" (when), it means "remember" (udhkur). And He says, after that, on the tongue of Abraham: "Rabb" (My Lord), and he did not say "Yā Allāh" (O God). That is because Abraham was raising his supplication to the Creator, the Sustainer, so he said "Rabbī" (my Lord) and did not say "Yā Allāh", because the gift of Allah is an obligation (taklīf), and in the face of an obligation there is a choice between doing and not doing, like His saying, glorified is He:

﴿And establish prayer...﴾ (43) (al-Baqarah).

As for the gift of lordship (rubūbiyyah), it is what sustains the life of those who pray and those who do not pray.

Abraham's request here does not come out of nowhere. We know that the Qur'an was revealed, and the first to hear it were the nobles of Quraysh, who enjoyed prestige and lordship over the Arabian Peninsula; no one dared to attack their caravans on their journeys of winter and summer, to Yemen and to Syria, and they had received this prestige from the Sacred House (al-Bayt al-Ḥarām).

Therefore, the Truth, glorified is He, spoke of the general blessing for every existing being whose ear awaits the call of Islam, and after that the Truth, glorified is He, speaks of the blessings that are specific, so He says:

﴿My Lord, make this city secure...﴾ (35) (Ibrāhīm).

This sentence occurs in surah al-Baqarah in another style, which is the saying of the Truth, glorified is He:

﴿And when Abraham said: "My Lord, make this city secure..."﴾ (126) (al-Baqarah).

The difference between "al-balad" (the city) and "baladan" (a city) requires us to explain it. "Baladan" means that the place was a barren wasteland (qafr),⁽²⁾ and Abraham prayed that this place would become a secure city, that is, that people would find it to live in, renew their needs and requirements, and that the means of livelihood there would be made easy. His supplication also included seeking security, that is, that nothing in it would threaten people's peace in their ordinary day and their means of livelihood.

The Truth, glorified is He, answered Abraham's supplication, and the place became a city; He made it secure with a general security, because a person in any part of the earth does not take a place to sit in, dwell and settle in unless he secures for himself the causes of safety from the requirements of life and from not being strongly terrified, and this security is required for every human being in any land.

Abraham, peace be upon him, made this supplication at the time he came to this place, and it was a valley without crops and without any requirements for life in it, so this was his supplication mentioned in surah al-Baqarah.

Here, however, the place had become a city, and the supplication for security was the second time; it is a call for a special security. In other places a tree may be cut down or game hunted, but in this place there is something very special: security for plants and for everything found in it. Even animals are not hunted in it, and even the perpetrator of a crime is not touched.⁽³⁾

Thus the first supplication for security differs from the second: the first is a supplication for general security, and the second is a supplication for special security. Every city may have general security, but the city of the Sacred House enjoys a security that encompasses all creatures.

Some superficial people say: since the Truth has made the House a sacred and secure sanctuary, why has what has happened for years, the attacks on people in the Sanctuary, occurred?

We say: Was the security of the Sanctuary a matter of (cosmic) creation, or a legislated obligation? It is a legislated obligation, which is open to being obeyed and open to being disobeyed.

His saying, glorified is He:

﴿And whoever enters it shall be secure...﴾ (97) (Āl ʿImrān).

means: O you who follow the religion of God, you must make those who enter the Sanctuary feel that they are in safety and security, and there is a difference between a legislated command and a cosmic command.

He, glorified is He, says on the tongue of Abraham:

﴿And keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols﴾ (35) (Ibrāhīm).

This statement carries a prophecy of what happened in the Sacred House at the hands of ʿAmr ibn Luḥayy, who introduced the worship of idols into the Kaʿba, and it is a statement that carries a prophecy from Abraham, peace be upon him.

One may ask: how does Abraham supplicate with this, when he is an infallible prophet? How does he ask the Truth to keep him away from worshipping idols?

I say: Does infallibility prevent a person from asking his Lord to continue in what he is upon? We receive, for example, the legislated command from Him, glorified is He:

﴿O you who have believed, believe in Allah and His Messenger...﴾ (136) (al-Nisāʾ).

and it is a command to persevere.

The Truth, glorified is He, also said on the tongue of His messenger Shuʿayb, peace be upon him:

﴿We would have invented a lie against Allah if we returned to your religion after Allah has saved us from it. And it is not for us to return to it unless Allah, our Lord, should will...﴾ (89) (al-Aʿrāf).

In this statement there is humble entreaty to the One who has bestowed upon us the blessing of faith, and in this noble statement also is the boundless power of the Truth, glorified is He.

We notice that the Truth, glorified is He, said here:

﴿And keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols﴾ (35) (Ibrāhīm).

The ṣanam (idol) is not the wathan (idol-stone). The one formed in the shape of a human is the ṣanam, while the piece of stone alone, which some of the people of jāhiliyyah singled out for worship, is the wathan.⁽⁴⁾

Here someone wanted to lead us out of this predicament, saying: disbelief is of two kinds: overt shirk (shirk jalī) and hidden shirk (shirk khafī). Overt shirk is that a person worships any being other than God, and hidden shirk is that a person sanctifies the intermediaries between himself and God, gives them more than they deserve, and attributes to them some of God's powers.

Abraham's supplication, peace be upon him, that he and his sons be kept away from worshipping idols requires us to understand the meaning of the word "sons" (abnāʾ). Abraham intended by his supplication his sons who would attain the rank of messengership and prophethood like him, for we know that some of his sons did worship idols and images.

The meaning of the word "sons" was explained by Him, glorified is He, in other places. We begin with His saying:

﴿And when Abraham was tested by his Lord with words⁽⁵⁾ and he fulfilled them...﴾ (124) (al-Baqarah).

That is: after God informed Abraham and charged him with the duties which God, glorified and exalted is He, had charged him with, perfectly, the Truth granted him to be an imam, so He, glorified is He, said:

﴿Indeed, I will make you a leader for the people...﴾ (124) (al-Baqarah).

That is: the basis of the imamate is Abraham, peace be upon him, performing every task completely, precisely and faithfully. If he is the constitution of God in creation, then we must be characterized by the character of God. We must not choose any person for any task to be its leader unless he is qualified for it and performs it well.

Let us recall His, may God's peace and blessings be upon him, saying:

"When trust is lost, then await the Hour." The questioner asked him about the time of the Hour's establishment: "And how is it lost?" He said: "When affairs are entrusted (wusside) to other than their people, then await the Hour."⁽⁶⁾⁽⁷⁾

That is because assigning any matter to someone other than its people is corruption in existence, for the principle in assigning any matter to any person is that it be with the aim that he carry out the matter as it should be. If the choice is bad, this person will become an example of evil, and the contagion of non-perfection will spread from him to others, and evil will spread in society. But if the matter is entrusted to one who is worthy of it, the situation is entirely different: placing a person in his fitting place balances the scales of justice, and in the balance of justice is the stability of time, place and the human being.

An example of this: the children who were raised in Saudi Arabia, and who saw that the hand of the thief is cut off, we did not find among them anyone who steals, because they were raised on the understanding that the thief's hand is cut off, and they understood that the Truth, glorified is He, in the moment He sets a harsh punishment, does not intend that the crime occurs, but rather that the crime does not occur.

When those who claim civilization ask: how does the Qur'an say:

﴿There is no compulsion in religion﴾ (256) (al-Baqarah).

and when you find someone who leaves the religion, you seize him, and some call for his execution?

To these I say: Is this matter counted against Islam, or in favor of Islam?

It is in favor of Islam, for this kind of zeal for the dignity of religion makes people fear entering the religion except after persuasion that leads to certainty, and certainty is reaching the true religion accompanied by evidence.

The Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth...﴾ (53) (Fuṣṣilat).

From this we know that one who enters Islam will sacrifice his life if he wants to leave it, because he left the certainty he entered by evidence.

When Abraham, peace be upon him, supplicated his Lord:

﴿My Lord, make this city secure and keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols﴾ (35) (Ibrāhīm).

he had succeeded in God's test for him, and had succeeded in performing what was entrusted to him completely; the Truth, glorified is He, willed for him to be an imam, and Abraham, peace be upon him, hoped that the imamate would be in his progeny, so he said:

﴿And of my descendants...﴾ (124) (al-Baqarah).

The answer came to him from the Truth, glorified is He:

﴿My covenant does not reach the wrongdoers﴾ (124) (al-Baqarah).

Thus the Truth, glorified is He, made clear that the sonship of the prophets is not sonship of flesh and blood, but sonship of following and emulation. We all know that the Truth, glorified is He, said to Noah about his son:⁽⁸⁾

﴿So do not ask Me about that of which you have no knowledge...﴾ (46) (Hūd).

And we know that the Messenger of Allah, may God's peace and blessings be upon him, said about Salman, who was Persian:

"Salman is one of us, the People of the House."⁽⁹⁾

In this is confirmation that the sonship of the prophets is sonship of following and emulation.

Al-Sha'rawi continues with Allah's account of Ibrahim's supplication (peace be upon him), where we find the Friend of the Most Merciful's awareness of what the idols do:

﴿My Lord, they have indeed led many of the people astray. So whoever follows me is of me, and whoever disobeys me — indeed You are Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

We know that the idols in themselves do not lead anyone astray(1), for they do not speak or converse with anyone. Rather, it is those who stand over them, on the claim that these idols possess divinity and that no obligation comes from them, who lead people astray and leave them as the common saying puts it: "left to the wind of their hair" (ʿala ḥalli shuʿūrihim).

Whoever dislikes following the teachings of the One, the Unique Creator, welcomes this misguidance.

Allah then follows what came on the tongue of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) after the supplication:

﴿So whoever follows me is of me, and whoever disobeys me — indeed You are Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ (Ibrahim)

These are follow-up statements on the matter of forgiveness and mercy after disobedience. Sometimes Allah, glory be to Him, follows it with:

﴿the Almighty, the All-Wise﴾ (al-Ma'idah, 118).

And sometimes He follows it with:

﴿the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾ (al-Zumar, 53).

This is because crimes differ in their degrees. There is the crime of supreme treason, or the crime of the summit, such as one who claims to be a god, or one whose followers say of him that he is a god without him having said so to them.

Jesus (peace be upon him) said, when Allah questioned him:

﴿Did you say to the people, "Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah"?...﴾ (al-Ma'idah, 116).

Then Jesus's words come:

﴿If I had said it, You would have known it. You know what is within myself, and I do not know what is within Yourself. Indeed, You are the Knower of the unseen.﴾ (al-Ma'idah, 116).

Jesus (peace be upon him) continues his speech:

﴿If You punish them, indeed they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, indeed You are the Almighty, the All-Wise.﴾ (al-Ma'idah, 118).

Thus might and forgiveness come after the mention of punishment. There are situations that call for might and wisdom, and situations that call for forgiveness and mercy, and no one is able to reverse the command of Allah concerning forgiveness or mercy, because He is Almighty and All-Wise.

As for His saying, the Truth:

﴿My Lord, they have indeed led many of the people astray...﴾ (Ibrahim).

It reflects attributes suited to the introductory statements of the verse, and confirms to us that the Qur'an is from the All-Wise, the All-Aware, and that Allah is the One who revealed the Qur'an to His servant:

﴿We will make you recite, and you will not forget﴾ (al-A'la, 6).

So what makes Him say in one verse:

﴿the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾ (al-Zumar, 53),

and in another:

﴿the Almighty, the All-Wise﴾ (al-Ma'idah, 118),

even though the meaning of the context might seem, outwardly, to suggest the opposite?

And what makes Him, glory be to Him, say in one verse, after reminding us that the blessings of Allah cannot be counted or enumerated:

﴿Indeed, mankind is truly a wrongdoer, a disbeliever﴾ (Ibrahim, 34),

and say in another verse, after reminding us of the blessings of Allah in the same wording:

﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (al-Nahl, 18).

Likewise His saying:

﴿No! Indeed, it is a reminder. So whoever wills may remember it﴾ (Abasa, 11–12),

and then His saying in another verse:

﴿Indeed, this is a reminder, so whoever wills may take to his Lord a way﴾ (al-Insan, 29).

All of this gives us the wisdom of the revelation, for every verse has a wisdom, and its revelation carries the secrets of its intended meaning.

All of this comes as confirmation of His saying, the Truth:

﴿We will make you recite, and you will not forget﴾ (al-A'la, 6).

Because Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, willed to send down the Qur'an to His Messenger and guaranteed that He would preserve it; and He will never let the place or position of any verse be forgotten, for the One who said:

﴿We will make you recite, and you will not forget﴾ (al-A'la, 6)

is the Truth, the Creator, the Able.

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on Surah 14, verse 37:

The Exalted says, after that, what Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said:

﴿Our Lord, I have settled some of my offspring in a valley without cultivation, by Your Sacred House, our Lord, that they may establish prayer. So make hearts among the people incline towards them and provide for them from the fruits, that they may be grateful.﴾ [14:37]

From the wording of this verse we understand that the place is not suitable for cultivation, for it is rocky land, not land that can be reclaimed. Ibrahim's words (peace be upon him):

﴿without cultivation..﴾ [14:37]

mean: there is no hope of cultivating it through human effort, and there is no means for provision to exist in this place except the bounty of the Lord. The choice of the place was not the result of a search by Ibrahim (peace be upon him); rather, it was by divine assignment. It was Allah, glory be to Him, who commanded him to raise the foundations of the Sacred House, and it is a place chosen by Allah, not chosen by Ibrahim (peace be upon him).

When Ibrahim (peace be upon him) says:

﴿by Your Sacred House..﴾ [14:37]

this signifies the basis of contentment with the assignment. Since this is a divine command that must be carried out with love, he receives two rewards: the reward of loving the assignment, and the reward of carrying it out.

We have an example in the story of the man whom al-Asma'i (1) met at the Sacred House, and who was saying: "O Allah, I have disobeyed You, but I love those who obey You, so make it a means of nearness for me." Al-Asma'i said, meaning that Allah must forgive this man for the goodness of his request, for he is a man who rejoiced in loving the assignment even though he did not perform it himself; rather, someone else performs it, and this makes him happy.

When the assignment is carried out by any person, it is a matter in the interest of all mankind. All of us say, when we pray and recite the Fatihah:

﴿You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help.﴾ [1:5]

That is: each of us places himself among the ranks of the worshippers, in the hope that Allah accepts from one of them, so we all enter into one transaction. Therefore I say to whoever commits a sin: you should not be angry, for there is one who obeys Allah; rather, rejoice in him, for your joy in the one who obeys Allah is evidence that you love the assignment, even though you cannot control yourself, and in this love there is honour for you.

Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said of the valley where the Almighty commanded him to raise the foundations of the Sacred House that it is a valley without cultivation. He came to this place to carry out the assignment of the Almighty, to the extent that his wife Hajar knew that settling in this place was by command of Allah, and she said: "Then He will not let us perish" (2).

Ibrahim (peace be upon him) presents the grounds for residing in this place and the reasons for his establishing the foundations as Allah willed, and he says:

﴿So make hearts among the people incline towards them..﴾ [14:37]

That is: the coming of people to this place will not be out of desire for tourism, but for the worship of His servants; since a House of Allah has been established in this place by Allah's choice, it must be worshipped in by Him.

Thus the grounds for undertaking to be present in a place that has none of the means or foundations of life become entirely clear. But the Almighty has commanded it, so the one who establishes prayer must establish a life, and the first foundation of life is food and drink.

For this reason Ibrahim (peace be upon him) supplicated:

﴿So make hearts among the people incline towards them..﴾ [14:37]

"Afida" (hearts) is the plural of "fu'ad" and is used for a group, and the connection of the heart with the pilgrims is a strong one, for the inclination of pilgrims is an inclination of hearts, not of purses. You find a person gathering the money for Hajj and he may deprive himself of many things in order to be granted the performance of that obligation (4).

The word "hawa" is composed of the letters hā', wāw and yā', and has several meanings. You may say "hawa" (هَوَى) or say "hawiya" (هَوِي). If you say "hawa yahwi" (هَوَى يهوي), it means to fall from a high place, without the will of the one falling, as if he were overpowered; and if you say "hawiya yahwa" (هَوِي يهوي), it means to love, and it results from the inclination of hearts, not the inclination of bodies.

Here the Almighty says:

﴿So make hearts among the people incline towards them, and provide for them from the fruits, that they may be grateful.﴾ [14:37]

They are in a place that cannot be cultivated. Allah, glory be to Him, accepted Ibrahim's supplication, and we find its practical fulfilment in His saying:

﴿Have We not established for them a secure sanctuary, to which fruits of every kind are brought as provision from Us..﴾ [28:57]

This was before any oil or other wealth was discovered. The word "yujba" (يُجبى) indicates that this provision coming from Allah is like a levy, a matter imposed. For example, you might be in al-Ta'if, where there are pomegranates and grapes, and you try to buy some, and someone tells you: this belongs to Makkah al-Mukarramah; if you want it, go there.

And in the phrase:

﴿fruits of every kind..﴾ [28:57]

there is something that arouses wonder and astonishment, for in Makkah you indeed find fruits of every kind, whether of agriculture or industry; there are the fruits of the four seasons, coming from every land, as a result of every environment sending some of its produce to Makkah.

In our present age we find the fruits of civilisational growth and minds that think, displayed in the markets of Makkah or Jeddah; indeed, you find the fruits of planning and capabilities that have been turned into tangible reality in every aspect of life there.

In the past, when we performed the Hajj, we used to take with us needles and thread, and table salt; and after most of the Arabian Peninsula was unified under the rule of the House of Saud and oil was discovered, we began to go there and bring back the luxuries of life.

Let us note the saying of the Almighty:

﴿So make hearts among the people incline towards them..﴾ [14:37]

The word "min" (from) makes clear that those whose hearts incline towards the place are a portion of the hearts of mankind. Some of the knowers of Allah said: had the text been "make hearts of the people incline towards them," we would have found the followers of other religions also entering the pilgrimage; but by the mercy of Allah, glory be to Him, the text came as:

﴿So make hearts from among the people incline towards them..﴾ [14:37]

so the pilgrimage was restricted to the Muslims.

2 He is: Abd al-Malik ibn Qurayb al-Asma'i al-Bahili, Abu Sa'id, born in Basra (122 AH), a transmitter of Arab lore, and one of the leading authorities in the science of language, poetry and regions; he was much given to wandering in the deserts. He died in Basra (216 AH) at the age of 94. [al-A'lam of al-Zirikli 4/162]
3 That is because Ibrahim (peace be upon him) brought Hajar and her suckling son Isma'il to Makkah, which had no one in it and no water. He placed them there, and placed beside them a bag containing dates and a waterskin containing water, then left them and went away. Hajar said: "O Ibrahim, where are you going, leaving us in this valley in which there is no human being or anything?" She said this to him repeatedly, but he did not turn to her. She said to him: "Did Allah command you this?" He said: "Yes." She said: "Then He will not let us perish." Recorded by al-Qurtubi in his tafsir (5/3707).
4 Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid said: had it said "afidat al-nas" (the hearts of mankind), Persia, Rome, the Turks, India, the Jews, the Christians and the Magians would have crowded upon it; but it says "min al-nas" (from among mankind), meaning the Muslims. Recorded by al-Qurtubi in his tafsir (5/3711), and al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (5/48).
5 Jaba yajba: to collect money or tribute, a collection. Allah says: ﴿yujba ilayhi thamarat kulli shay'.. ﴾ [28:57], meaning: fruits and many goods are gathered to the sacred Makkan precinct and driven to it. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/117]
6 Al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (5/48) quoted from al-Suddi, attributed to Ibn Abi Hatim, that he said in the tafsir of this verse: "Draw the hearts of people towards them, for wherever the heart inclines, the body goes; therefore there is no believer except that his heart is attached to love of the Ka'bah."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 14, verse 38:

Then Allah, glorified and exalted, continues what was said on the tongue of Ibrahim, peace be upon him:

﴿Our Lord, You know what we conceal and what we declare, and nothing is hidden from Allah on the earth or in the heaven.﴾ (14:38)

After Ibrahim, peace be upon him, was reassured that this land has a general security and a specific security, and was reassured about the means of sustenance, and that everything is from Allah, after all of that the matter that had been preoccupying him returned to him, namely the matter of leaving Hajar and Isma'il in this place.

Some of the exegetes said: the plural pronoun in His saying, exalted is He:

﴿You know what we conceal and what we declare...﴾ (14:38)

is intended to refer to what he harbored of love for Hajar and Isma'il, and what he displayed of harshness toward them before Sarah. It is as if these inner feelings returned to him at the moment he began the farewell greeting to Hajar and her son Isma'il.

We say: Hajar too was living through a difficult situation, for she had been placed in a place with no crops and no water, and it is as if she had suppressed her human impulses throughout that period and endured patiently.

When Ibrahim came to bid her farewell, she said to him: "Where will you leave us? Is it by your own opinion or by the command of your Lord?" Ibrahim, peace be upon him, said to her: "Rather, it is by the command of Allah." She said: "Then He will not neglect us."

Hajar became certain that what she had said had been fulfilled, and that Allah had not neglected them. When her only son became thirsty, she ran between al-Safa and al-Marwa seeking water; but she saw the water gushing beneath the feet of her son, in the place where she had left him, and from that time the well of Zamzam(1) began to give its water to people, waters that never run dry(2).

Thus the saying of Ibrahim, peace be upon him, is realized, that Allah knows what we keep secret and what we declare. For every declared matter was not declared except after it had been hidden. Although Allah is the Unseen, His knowledge does not remain limited to the unseen; rather it encompasses the outward and the inward world, and everything enclosed in the heavens or the earth is known to Allah, because what you regard as unseen in your mind is known to Allah before your mind moves toward it.

For this reason He, glorified, says elsewhere:

﴿And if you speak aloud, then indeed He knows the secret and what is more hidden.﴾ (20:7)

So if the secret is what you confided to another, and it came out of you because you entrusted the other person not to say it, or if the secret is what you concealed within yourself, then Allah is the Knower of it in both cases.

The Qur'an says:

﴿And when the Prophet confided to one of his wives a statement...﴾ (66:3)

That is: the secret was with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and it passed to some of his wives. "Al-akhfa" (what is more hidden) is what exists before you disclose the secret, and you conceal it and do not disclose it.

He, glorified, knows this secret and what you conceal, that is, the secret you have not told anyone, and He knows it even before it becomes a secret.

1 It is said: "Zamzam water": abundant, between brackish and sweet. [Lisan al-Arab, entry: zamzam]
2 Nadaba al-ma': it went into the earth and receded deep. And nadaba al-bi'r: its water was drawn out and dried up. [Lisan al-Arab, entry: nadaba]

Al-Sha'rawi, Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66), on surah 14, verse 39:

Almighty God says what Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said, in supplication and in praise of Him:

﴿All praise is due to God, who has given me, in old age, Isma'il and Ishaq. Indeed, my Lord is Hearer of supplication.﴾ (39)

Al-wahb (bestowal) is a gift from one who gives without any return from you. All offspring are a gift; were they not a gift, they would be routine between spouses, and wherever there are spouses, offspring exist. Therefore God said:

﴿He bestows female offspring on whom He wills, and bestows male offspring on whom He wills, or pairs them, males and females, and makes whom He wills barren. Indeed, He is All-Knowing, All-Powerful.﴾ (42:49-50)

The evidence that offspring are a gift is what God willed concerning Zakariyya (peace be upon him). He asked God to grant him a boy who would inherit him, although he had reached extreme old age (ʿitiyy) and his wife was barren. Zakariyya was amazed at this, because he had been able to beget with strength. On this same meaning, the Truthful One says:

﴿Thus said your Lord: "It is easy for Me, and I created you before, when you were nothing."﴾ (19:9)

This means that Zakariyya did not enter into the means, the causes and the laws.

God has named offspring a gift; therefore we must thank God for His gift, and His gift must not be rejected. If He bestows daughters on you, then it is "on the eye and the head" (gladly accepted). For whoever accepts God's gift of daughters with contentment, God grants him young men who marry the girls, and who become more obedient to him than his own sons, although he did not toil in raising them.

Each of us sees this in his surroundings: whoever has begotten sons keeps watching whether his son will marry one who snatches him away and makes him more obedient to her than to him.

If He bestows sons on you, then it is also "on the eye and the head," and you must ask God that your son be of righteous offspring. If He bestows on you both males and females, then you should thank Him and ask God to help you raise them.

As for the one whom the Truthful One has made barren, he should thank his Lord, because barrenness too is a gift from Him, glory be to Him. We have seen the son who kills his father and mother, and we have seen the daughter who disowns her father and mother.

If the barren one accepts God's gift in this and declares this acceptance to himself and to those around him, then God, Exalted, makes all people look at him with the gaze of children toward a father, and every young man who sees him says to him: "Do you want something, uncle so-and-so?" and everyone serves him with pure affection.

Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said to the Truthful One:

﴿All praise is due to God, who has given me, in old age..﴾ (14:39)

Thanks for a gift, as we have known, takes the form of the giving of offspring in youth or in old age.

The people of tafsir say concerning:

﴿in old age..﴾ (14:39)

that he thanks God for His giving him Isma'il and Ishaq although he was old.

And why does God use ʿalā ("on"), which has three letters, instead of maʿa ("with"), and did not say: "All praise is due to God, who has given me, with old age, Isma'il and Ishaq"?

I say: ʿalā indicates elevation. Old age is weakness, but God's will is stronger than weakness. Had He said "maʿa al-kibar" (with old age), the sense of accompaniment would not necessarily imply strength. But His saying:

﴿who has given me, in old age..﴾ (14:39)

makes God's power in giving rise above old age.

When Ibrahim (peace be upon him) says this, he is thanking God for answering what he had said earlier:

﴿Indeed, I have settled some of my offspring in a valley without cultivation..﴾ (14:37)

That is, he had prayed that he would have offspring.

The Almighty ends the verse with Ibrahim's words:

﴿Indeed, my Lord is Hearer of supplication.﴾ (14:39)

1 Ibn ʿAbbas said: Ibrahim was ninety-nine years old when Isma'il was born to him, and Ishaq came to him when he was one hundred and twelve years old. [Tafsir al-Qurtubi 5/3713].
2 ʿatā ʿatwan wa-ʿitiyyan: he grew old and aged, and his freshness and vigour departed. The Exalted said about Zakariyya: ﴿And you have reached extreme old age (ʿitiyyan)﴾ (19:8). [al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/6].

Then He, glorified is He, says after that:

﴿My Lord, make me an establisher of prayer, and [among] my descendants. Our Lord, and accept my supplication.﴾ [14:40]

It is as if Abraham, peace be upon him, when he asked for the establishing of prayer, was asking about a matter that concerns God's method, and he was asking God to accept it. That is because his other requests he made out of his human nature; what he asked for might be harm or good, but the request that He make him and his descendants establishers of prayer is a request for good.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 14, verse 41:

The supplication continues in the words of Allah, glorified is He, on the tongue of Ibrahim, peace be upon him:

﴿Our Lord, forgive me and my parents and the believers on the Day when the reckoning will be established.﴾

We know that asking forgiveness from one who is protected from sin (ma'sum) is a notice of the absoluteness of Allah's power over the cosmos. This is because Allah's choosing of a messenger, any messenger, does not exempt the chosen messenger from caution and from seeking forgiveness. Here is our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), saying: "Indeed I seek forgiveness from Allah in the day and the night a hundred times."(1)

Seeking forgiveness from Allah, if it is not for a sin, as is the case with the protected messengers, is then part of good manners (adab) with Allah, because the Creator, glorified and exalted is He, deserves from us more than what He has obligated us to. So if we cannot perform the recommended acts (mandubat) and the voluntary acts (tatawwu'at), then let us ask Allah, glorified is He, to forgive us.

Among us is one who cannot perform the obligatory duties (fara'id); so let him ask Allah to forgive him. For this reason it is said: "The good deeds of the righteous (abrar) are the misdeeds of those brought near (muqarrabin)."(2)

And Allah, glorified is He, says to His Messenger (ﷺ):

﴿That Allah may forgive you your past sin and what is to come, and complete His favour upon you and guide you to a straight path.﴾ (al-Fath).

For this reason I always say: the Truth, of majestic essence, deserves to be worshipped beyond what He has obligated. So if we limit ourselves to performing what He has obligated, it is as if we have not rendered full thanks. What then of us, if such a state is the conduct of the messengers, especially since Allah, glorified is He, has granted them a distinction above His creation? Should they not increase Him in thanks and in seeking forgiveness?

We note that the seeking of forgiveness here has included the parents and the believers:

﴿Our Lord, forgive me and my parents and the believers on the Day when the reckoning will be established.﴾ (Ibrahim).

Man, as we know, has an original existence from Adam, peace be upon him, and a direct existence from his two parents. Since man came into this world by means of his parents, and has become a believer, he prays for them for forgiveness; or: the model (uswa) came from them, therefore he prays for them for forgiveness.

Man prays for the believers for forgiveness, because they were companions (suhba) and exemplars for him, and he counselled them and they counselled him toward truth and patience. It is as if Ibrahim, peace be upon him, the one making the supplication, is praying for the believers among his descendants, and this is a supplication and an intercession from him for those who believed, and he hopes that Allah, glorified is He, will accept it.

1 Related by al-Darimi in his Sunan (2/302), and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak (2/457), who said: "Its chain is sound, though they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not narrate it," and Ahmad in his Musnad (5/394), from the hadith of Hudhayfah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "There was a sharpness in my tongue toward my family, and it did not go beyond them to others, so I asked the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: 'Where are you from seeking forgiveness? Indeed I seek forgiveness from Allah every day a hundred times.'"..
2 The righteous (al-abrar) and those brought near (al-muqarrabun) are both from the people of Paradise, but the righteous are lower in rank than those brought near. Allah has spoken of the two categories. Of the brought near He said: ﴿And the foremost, the foremost, those are the ones brought near, in gardens of delight, a multitude of the former peoples and a few of the later ones, on couches woven with gold, reclining upon them facing one another, there will circulate among them immortal youths﴾ (al-Waqi'ah), and the verses. As for the righteous, He said of them: ﴿And the companions of the right hand, what are the companions of the right hand? Among lote-trees without thorns, and banana-trees arranged in tiers, and extended shade﴾ (al-Waqi'ah), and the verses. Because of the greatness of the rank of those brought near, it has been said: the good deeds that the righteous perform, by which they deserve the bliss of Paradise, are misdeeds compared with what those brought near perform..
3 Al-Qurtubi mentioned in his tafsir (5/3714) two other readings of this word:
(Walidi), meaning his father. This is the reading of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and that was before it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah.
(Waladayya), meaning his two sons. This is the reading of Ibrahim al-Nakha'i and Yahya ibn Ya'mur. For this reason it has been said that he meant his two sons: Isma'il and Ishaq..

And Allah, glory be to Him, says after this:

﴿And do not think that Allah is unaware of what the wrongdoers do. He only delays them until a Day when eyes will stare fixedly.﴾

After Allah, glory be to Him, had mentioned and explained the general blessings upon the universe, and the particular blessings He bestowed upon those who settled in Makkah and upon their descendants who stood against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in obstinate opposition, He then sent this verse as consolation and solace for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ):

﴿And do not think that Allah is unaware of what the wrongdoers do...﴾ (Ibrahim).

The backdrop of the imagery that preceded it includes the beginning of the formation of this place in which they were brought into being, and the manner in which blessings came to those who settled in this place, where fruits are brought to them, and the blessing of awe that they enjoy, as Allah overwhelms those who oppose them, such as Abrahah and his companions:

﴿And made them like eaten straw.﴾ (al-Fil).

Immediately after this verse, He, may He be glorified, says:

﴿For the accustomed security of the Quraysh, their accustomed security in the caravan of winter and summer, let them worship the Lord of this House, who has fed them against hunger and made them safe from fear.﴾ (Quraysh).

Despite all this, they stood against the call of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with denial, obstinacy, confrontation and ingratitude, and they sought the help of every enemy of Islam to fight this religion. Therefore, Allah here gives consolation to the Noble Messenger:

﴿And do not think that Allah is unaware of what the wrongdoers do...﴾

(Ibrahim).

Why? The answer comes in the second half of the verse:

﴿He only delays them until a Day when eyes will stare fixedly.﴾ (Ibrahim).

And His saying, the Truth:

﴿And do not think...﴾ (Ibrahim).

That is: do not suppose. Here, "hasiba" is not from counting and reckoning, but from "hasiba, yahsabu" (to think, suppose). And His saying that clarifies this matter:

﴿Do people think that they will be left to say, "We believe," and will not be tested?﴾ (al-'Ankabut).

That is: do people suppose. So "hasiba, yahsabu" is not from counting, but from supposing. Ḥusbān is a verbal relation that is not certain but is more probable.

As for the heedlessness (ghafla) that Allah negates from Himself, it is forgetting something due to lack of alertness or attention. Obviously and self-evidently, this cannot be attributed to Him, glory be to Him, for He is the Self-Subsisting (al-Qayyum) whom neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes.

Here Allah, the Truth, addresses His Messenger and, by extension, the believers with him. When Allah addresses His Messenger (ﷺ), He is at the same time addressing everyone who believed in him.

But did the Messenger think that Allah was heedless?

No. And let us note that when Allah gives a directive, the directive may carry a command that a person carries out in action, and Allah asks him to persist in that action.

For example: when you say "he does not drink wine" (meaning, "do not drink wine") and he does not drink wine, then by your saying this you are asking him to continue not drinking wine. That is: persist in what you are doing, in the case of a command by action, or in abstention, in the case of a prohibition.

Can heedlessness be attributed to Allah?

I say: when you see an attribute that exists in human beings but does not exist in the Truth, glory be to Him, you must interpret the matter in terms of the perfections that belong to Allah.

Whoever commits injustice will receive punishment for it. When the punishment is delayed, those who witnessed the act of injustice ask one another in whispers: "Has the injustice committed by so-and-so been forgotten? Is there heedlessness in the matter?"

In their questions they want to declare their position regarding the one who committed the sin and the necessity of punishing him. On this basis we understand the word:

﴿heedless﴾ (Ibrahim).

In this verse it means "one who postpones the punishment."

As for those who ask such questions, they should remember the saying of the Truth:

﴿And I give them respite; indeed, My plan is firm.﴾ (al-A'raf).

On this basis, there is no heedlessness, but there is a postponement of punishment for these wrongdoers. This is because injustice means taking a right from its owner and giving it to another, or taking it for oneself.

If the injustice is in a matter of creed, it is shirk (association of partners with Allah), which is the greatest crime. If you commit injustice in a major sin (kabira), this is fisq (grave transgression). And if you commit injustice in a minor sin (saghira), this is merely injustice (zulm).

For this reason we find that the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted be He, mentions a ruling appropriate to each of the three situations. He says about the one who overlooks the criminalisation of shirk:

﴿And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, those are the disbelievers.﴾ (al-Ma'idah).

And He says about the criminalisation of a major sin:

﴿And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, those are the defiantly disobedient.﴾ (al-Ma'idah).

And He says about one who overlooks the criminalisation of a minor sin, with the rulings of the religion appropriate to it:

﴿And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, those are the wrongdoers.﴾

(al-Ma'idah).

If a person is judged, and the judgement involves several rulings, then the ruling depends on what it is that he is judged for.

When we consider this matter of injustice, we find that the wrongdoer requires a person wronged. If the injustice is—God forbid—the greatest injustice, which is associating partners with Allah, then according to the scholars this injustice divides into three types:

The first type: denying the existence of Allah and His divinity without attributing it to anyone else. This is atheism (ilhad), and it is an injustice against what is obligatory concerning His existence, glory be to Him.

The second type: acknowledging the divinity of Allah while associating others with Him in divinity. This shirk is an injustice to the Truth concerning His essence and His unique singularity.

The third type: the claim that Allah is composed of parts. This is an injustice to Allah concerning the oneness of His essence.

Some of the knowers (al-'arifin) say: the first right in existence is His existence, glory be to Him.

Among them is the poet who said:

The first right in existence is its existence,
and all the rights of the universe are drawn from Him.
He is not one who is combined, as the polytheist says,
nor is He in parts, O beauty of my faith.

The injustice mentioned in the verse we are reflecting upon is the greatest injustice: an injustice in the divine creed. Along with it is another injustice, the injustice against the Messenger (ﷺ). The poet sums up their injustice towards the Messenger (ﷺ) by saying: "You called him trustworthy when he was young, and the trustworthy is not one accused."

They had named the Messenger (ﷺ) "the trustworthy" before the prophethood. After the prophethood they stripped him of this description, while before the prophethood they had described him as "the truthful." They never once said about him, before the prophethood, that he was a sorcerer, nor did they accuse him of madness before the prophethood.

How could he have had the attributes of truthfulness and of speaking the truth, and of being spoken of as having soundness of judgement, and yet you strip these from him after the prophethood?

How could he have had those attributes before the prophethood, and yet you strip them from him after the prophethood?

This is the injustice of depriving someone of perfection. The Messenger (ﷺ) had perfection before he was sent, and you wronged him after the prophethood by denying him that perfection. It is a double injustice.

For you had already acknowledged his trustworthiness before the prophethood, but after the prophethood you denied his trustworthiness. He was truthful before the prophethood, and after it you said he was not truthful.

He had no attribute of deficiency before the prophethood, yet you attributed to him a deficient attribute, such as your saying: "sorcerer," "soothsayer," "madman." In this there is injustice to the Messenger (ﷺ).

This is also an injustice to the society in which you live, for whoever wants the continuation of tyranny through a word of disbelief, and wants to remain in power, exploitation and domination over others, all of that is an injustice to society. And above that, it is an injustice to oneself, for whoever does this may obtain a small pleasure while depriving himself of a great pleasure, the pleasure of living under the way of Allah. The saying of the Most Merciful Truth applies to him:

﴿And We did not wrong them, but they were wronging themselves.﴾ (al-Nahl).

Beyond the injustice to oneself and the injustice to society, there is an injustice that this type of person commits against the whole universe, in what is below humanity: inanimate objects, animals and plants. This is because when a human being is not upon the way of his Creator, while the whole universe is subjected to the way of the Creator, that human will not respect this in his dealings with the universe. And He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And there is not a thing but that it exalts His praise...﴾ (al-Isra').

When everything in the universe glorifies Him, a human being who does not follow the way of Allah stands out from it. The whole universe dislikes him. Thus the human being wrongs himself and also wrongs the universe.

Thus we have come to know the greatest injustice in denying divinity, or associating partners with Him, glory be to Him, or imagining that He is composed of parts; the injustice of stripping the Messenger of perfection, though he is the intermediary who brought the news of faith; and the injustice to the whole universe, because the whole universe, in all its kinds, glorifies Allah.

And the saying of Allah, the Truth:

﴿And do not think that Allah is unaware of what the wrongdoers do...﴾

(Ibrahim).

In it we find the word "ya'malu" (does). We know that there is a difference between "'amila" and "fa'ala." "Fa'ala" is the performance of all the limbs, except the tongue, whose act is called "qawl" (saying).

The action of every limb is named by its own act, while the act of the tongue has a name of its own. This is because what throws people face-down into the Fire is only the harvest of their tongues. "Fi'l" and "qawl" are both included under the word "'amal" (action).

Here, in the verse we are reflecting upon, Allah says "ya'malu" (does), because the polytheists who received the Qur'an were spreading agitation about Islam and the Messenger (ﷺ) by means of speech, and all the acts they carried out arose from incitement by speech.

This noble verse, in which He, glory be to Him, confirms that He gives them time for their sins so that the punishment may also be fully established, is followed by His saying:

﴿He only delays them until a Day when eyes will stare fixedly.﴾ (Ibrahim).

We know that some of the signs confirming the nearness of the victory of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had already occurred to them. Their chieftains and some of their leaders were killed at Badr, and their great men were taken captive. Thus Allah willed to bring the promise or the threat, and He brought the matter that encompasses all listeners, which is the punishment of the Hereafter, if they persisted in shirk and in resisting the message.

And: ﴿Eyes will stare fixedly﴾ (Ibrahim).

It means: opened wide, in such a way that they do not turn to the right or the left, from the terror of what they see. The eye's not turning may also be from the intensity of the beauty of what it sees. What distinguishes the two is a particular state that belongs to the creation of Allah alone, and He is the one who creates it.

When you see a person terrified from excessive fear, his face takes on the shape of that fear. But one who looks at something beautiful, and whose eyes are fixed upon it, has features that harmonise with the satisfaction of gazing at beauty. This is why the poet says:

The beauty of the one I love is fixed in my gaze,
so would that nothing else could replace it.

We can distinguish between the one who is frightened and the one who enjoys, by the features of the face, whether relaxed or terrified.

We know that sight is the child of mirrors. When mirrors multiply, sight moves between them. Therefore the person who sees is always dispersed among mirrors, and his mind moves from here to there.

As for those whom Allah has blessed with the restraint of their sight, the blind, the mirrors do not occupy them. This is why we find them the most eager of people for knowledge, since their minds are not occupied with anything else, and the focal point of each one's awareness receives through the ear whatever settles in it.

For this reason they are called "chests of knowledge" when they wish to learn. None of those among them who learn is ever empty, just like a chest that never empties.

No one controls the emotion arising from instincts except Allah. You do not tell yourself "be angry" or "laugh," because He, glory be to Him, is the one who holds that power, and He says:

﴿And it is He who makes people laugh and weep.﴾ (al-Najm).

Laughing and weeping are involuntary matters in which no one has any say.

We find the Truth, glory be to Him, saying in another place in the Qur'an:

﴿And when the eyes are dazzled...﴾ (al-Ahzab).

So at times the eyes stare fixedly, and terror overtakes their owners so that they cannot turn away from the frightful scene. At other times the eyes dart about, as if seeking an outlet or a way of escape, and find none.

6 That is: O beautiful religion of Islam, which came from Allah affirming His existence without partner in dominion and without being composed of parts. It affirmed for Him, glory be to Him, the necessity of His existence, the oneness of His uniqueness, and the oneness of His essence. (ʿ).
7 "Kabba al-shay'u yakubbuhu": he overturned it. "Kabbahu li-wajhihi fa-inkabba": he threw him down on his face, so he fell prone. [Lisan al-'Arab, entry: kabb].
8 It is narrated from Mu'adh ibn Jabal that he said: "O Prophet of Allah, will we be held accountable for what we say?" He said: "May your mother be bereft of you, O Mu'adh! Do people get thrown on their faces or on their noses into the Fire except for the harvest of their tongues?" Narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad (5/231, 236) and al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan (2616), who said: "Hasan sahih."
9 "Arjafa al-qawm": when the people plunged into bad news and the mention of trials. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And the agitators in the city...﴾ (al-Ahzab, 60), who are those who fabricate false reports that cause turmoil among the people. [Lisan al-'Arab, entry: rajafa].
10 "Zaagh al-basar": the sight was disturbed and did not perceive what it saw correctly, or it deviated from its aim and saw nothing. "Zayagh al-absar": its disturbance due to intense terror. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/294].

Al-Sha'rawi continues describing the state of those whose eyes are fixed in terror:

Almighty Allah says:

"Hastening forward, with heads raised, their gaze not returning to them, and their hearts void." (Ibrahim 14:43)

Al-muhti' (the one hastening) is the one who appears, due to his extreme haste, as though his neck has been stretched out, for the muhti' is one who has length in his neck. It is as though the punishment draws the one being punished towards it, bringing him near, so he is pushed with harshness and roughness into the torment. Allah, glorified is He, says:

"They will be pushed headlong into the fire of Hell, a violent pushing." (al-Tur 52:13)

It is as though there are those who push them forcefully towards their painful fate. And they are:

"...with heads raised..." (Ibrahim 14:43)

That is, raising their heads from extreme astonishment at the terror of the punishment that awaits them.

In another place Allah, the Truth, depicts them:

"Indeed, We have put shackles around their necks, reaching to the chins, so they are held with their heads raised." (Ya-Sin 36:8)

Thus their image is frightening from extreme humiliation: the gaze of each of them is fixed upon the punishment, drawn towards it with a speed he cannot control, his head raised from extreme dread, and held up (muqmah) by the shackles.

None of them can close his eyelids, as though they are held open against his will. And his heart is "void" (hawa'), meaning that nothing is able to enter it.

We notice this when we place an empty bottle in water: bubbles of air emerge opposite the entry of water from its mouth.

We know that the heart of the believer is full of faith; as for the disbelieving atheist, at such a moment he reviews his history with God and with religion, and finds in it nothing that brings tranquillity. Thus he discovers that his heart is empty and vacant, not reassured by anything with which he confronts the moment of reckoning.

We find some of those who have witnessed the moments of dying of others saying of the death of a believer: "his face was radiant and his features shining." As for what they say of the moment of death of a disbeliever, they describe the hideousness of his features at that moment.

The reason for this is that a person in such moments reviews his history with God and sees the film of his whole deed. Whoever has spent his life pleasing God must feel comfort; and whoever has spent his life as a disbelieving atheist must feel the terrifying fate that awaits him.

Therefore Allah, glorified is He, says:

"Faces that day will be radiant, looking towards their Lord. And faces that day will be gloomy, thinking that a calamity will be inflicted upon them." (al-Qiyamah 75:22–25)

2. da'hu yad'uhu: pushed him harshly. al-da''a: driving away and pushing with rebuke and scolding. [Lisan al-Arab, root d-'-'']
3. al-dhaqn: the joining of the two jaws below the face; it is used figuratively for the hair growing on it, and may be used for the whole face. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/243]
4. al-muqmah: the submissive, humbled one who can hardly raise his gaze. al-Azhari said: He, Mighty and Majestic, meant that when their hands were chained at their necks, the shackles raised their chins and heads upward like camels raising their heads. [Lisan al-Arab, root q-m-h]

Allah the Exalted says after that:

﴿And warn mankind of the Day when the punishment will come to them, and those who did wrong will say, "Our Lord, respite us for a short term; we will answer Your call and follow the messengers." Had you not sworn before that there would be for you no cessation?﴾ [14:44]

This is an address from Allah the Exalted to His Messenger ﷺ, that he should warn them of the necessity of preparing for the Day of Resurrection, and that it is coming without doubt.

The word "yawm" (day) is an adverb of time (zarf zaman), and an adverb of time must have an event occurring within it. The Day of Resurrection is not a place for warning or glad tidings, because warning or glad tidings must occur in the time of accountability in the life of this world.

Thus, what is warned of is frightening them about what will happen to them on this Day. What will happen to them is the punishment; it is as if it were a timed bomb that, as soon as the Day of Resurrection comes, explodes in their faces.

Here the people of wrongdoing at the summit of belief, the wrongdoing of opposing the message, and the wrongdoing against the universe that glorifies Allah, say:

﴿Our Lord, respite us for a short term; we will answer Your call and follow the messengers...﴾ [14:44] (Ibrahim).

They ask for the postponement of the punishment for a simple respite, in which they would prove that they will answer the call and obey the Messenger. By this they seek to postpone their reckoning.

So the answer comes from Allah the Exalted:

﴿Had you not sworn before that there would be for you no cessation?﴾ [14:44] (Ibrahim).

You had already sworn that Allah would not resurrect those who die, and Allah the Exalted has stated what you said:

﴿And they swore by Allah their most emphatic oaths that Allah will not resurrect those who die...﴾ [16:38] (al-Nahl).

Whenever you see the word "bala" (yes indeed) after a negation, it means the denial of what came before it. In the verse we are reflecting upon, they thought that they would not be resurrected, and they thought that after death they would become dust; they are the ones who said:

﴿There is nothing but our life of this world; we die and we live, and we will not be resurrected.﴾ [23:37] (al-Mu'minun).

Thus they affirmed to themselves that there is no resurrection after life, and after resurrection every one of them will say:

﴿Would that I had been dust!﴾ [78:40] (al-Naba').

Or: they thought that those whom Allah had blessed in this world would not be deprived of blessing in the Hereafter, as Allah the Exalted cited this parable in His saying:

﴿And strike for them an example of two men: We granted one of them two gardens of grapevines, and We surrounded them with date palms and placed between them crops. Each of the two gardens produced its fruit and did not fail in anything. And We caused a river to gush forth within them. And he had fruit, so he said to his companion while speaking with him, "I am greater than you in wealth and stronger in men." And he entered his garden while he was unjust to himself. He said, "I do not think this will ever perish, and I do not think the Hour will occur. And even if I should be returned to my Lord, I will surely find better than this as a destination."﴾ [18:32–36] (al-Kahf).

Whoever says this understood that he would die, but he imagined that his garden would remain as it is, and he denied the establishment of the Hour, and said: "Even if the Hour is established and I am returned to God, I will find better than this garden of mine."

He claims that while he has not presented faith in God so as to find it in the Hereafter. Therefore he is among those who denied cessation, i.e., resurrection anew, and fell into the circle of those who did not believe in the resurrection. Allah the Exalted had earlier stated what He relates of their speech:

﴿When we have become lost in the earth, shall we indeed be in a new creation?﴾ [32:10] (al-Sajdah).

Allah the Exalted presents to us a dialogue between Him and those who denied resurrection, so He, glory be to Him and exalted, says:

﴿They will say, "Our Lord, You have caused us to die twice and given us life twice, and we have acknowledged our sins. Is there any way to get out?"﴾ [40:11] (Ghafir).

Allah the Exalted responds to them:

﴿That is because when Allah was invoked alone, you disbelieved; but when partners were associated with Him, you believed. So judgment belongs to Allah, the Most High, the Most Great.﴾ [40:12] (Ghafir).

In another place in the Qur'an we find a dialogue and a plea from them to Allah, they say:

﴿Our Lord, we have seen and heard, so return us that we may work righteousness...﴾ [32:12] (al-Sajdah).

And the response of Allah the Exalted comes to them:

﴿So taste [the punishment] for your forgetting the meeting of this your Day; indeed, We have forgotten you...﴾ [32:14] (al-Sajdah).

In a third place, one of them says at death:

﴿My Lord, send me back, that I might do righteousness in that which I left behind...﴾ [23:99–100] (al-Mu'minun).

The response of Allah the Exalted comes:

﴿No! It is but a word he is saying...﴾ [23:100] (al-Mu'minun).

And after they enter the Fire they say:

﴿Our Lord, bring us out of it, and if we return [to disbelief], then indeed we will be wrongdoers.﴾ [23:107] (al-Mu'minun).

Allah the Exalted says:

﴿He will say, "Remain in it with contempt, and do not speak to Me."﴾ [23:108] (al-Mu'minun).

In another place they say, as they cry out (istiṣrākh) in the Fire:

﴿Our Lord, bring us out; we will do righteousness other than what we used to do...﴾ [35:37] (Fatir).

The response comes from Allah the Exalted:

﴿Did We not give you a life long enough that whoever would be reminded could be reminded therein, and the warner had come to you? So taste [the punishment], for there are not for the wrongdoers any helpers.﴾ [35:37] (Fatir).

We notice that in all the verses of supplication to Allah that they be returned to the life of this world, they say "Our Lord" (rabbana), and they forgot that they are being taken to punishment for violations of divinity (al-uluhiyyah); that is because the lordship (al-rububiyyah) and its bounty were yours in the world, and Allah the Exalted did not deprive you of anything despite your disbelief.

Such is the condition of those who swore that Allah the Exalted would not resurrect them, who denied the Day of Resurrection, and that there would be for them no cessation; i.e., no resurrection and no rising.
