1. Al-jannah: a garden with much dense foliage that covers the ground. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/133]
2. Dalla fi al-ard: died and became dust, so that nothing of his creation was distinguished. [Lisan al-Arab, root ḍ-l-l]
3. Ukhsa'u: withdraw and keep away from me in the Fire and do not speak to me. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/192] Al-khasi'': the humbled, abased one. [al-Mu'jam al-Wajiz, root kh-s-'']
4. Istaṣrakha al-qawm wa-tasarakhū: they cried out for help. Al-istiṣrākh: mutual shouting. [Lisan al-Arab, root ṣ-r-kh]

Al-Sha'rawi continues with the noble word of Allah, the Exalted:

﴿And you dwelt in the dwellings of those who wronged themselves, and it became clear to you how We dealt with them, and We set forth for you the parables.﴾

Sukun (سكون) is settling down in a thing with no disturbance, and we know that a wife in marriage is considered a sakan (a place of rest), and the house is a sakan. Here the Truth, the Exalted, speaks of the dwellings of those who wronged themselves, meaning: you did not take warning from the precedents, which should not have escaped you. You travel on your summer and winter journeys past the cities of Salih, you see the remains of those who wronged themselves through disbelief and polytheism, you pass by al-Ahqaf(2), and you see what befell the people of 'Ad.

All of these received punishment from Allah, whether by the violent (ṣarṣar) wind(3) that was raging, or: He, the Exalted, sent upon them a hasib(4) from the sky, or: He sent down upon them the Cry; or: He drowned them, like the family of Pharaoh, and each people was seized for their sin.

Allah fulfilled His promise regarding the punishment of this world. So why do you not take a lesson from that, and [why not consider] that He, the Exalted, is truthful when He speaks of the punishment of the Hereafter?

Here the Truth, the Exalted, said:

﴿And you dwelt in the dwellings of those who wronged themselves...﴾ (Ibrahim).

In another verse He, the Exalted, says:

﴿And indeed you pass by them in the morning, [137] and at night. Will you not then reason?﴾ (As-Saffat).

That is: you pass by those places which some of those who came before you built, and who wronged themselves with disbelief; and the Truth, the Exalted, sent down punishment upon them. For this reason He says, in the verse which is the subject of our reflections:

﴿And it became clear to you how We dealt with them, and We set forth for you the parables.﴾

(Ibrahim).

Indeed, when you walk in the land of the people of 'Ad, and see their civilisation, of which the Truth, the Exalted, said:

﴿Iram, with lofty pillars [7], the like of which was not created in the lands [8]﴾

(Al-Fajr).

It is a civilisation whose remains we have not yet discovered; they are still buried, and every buried thing in the earth is by the act of the wrath of heaven; heaven sets an appointed time for its uncovering so that the people of the earth may take warning. This uncovering happens whenever disbelief increases and spreads.

It has happened that we discovered the civilisation of Thamud, and likewise the civilisation of the Pharaohs, which preceded all civilisations in sciences and technology, yet despite that, the people of that civilisation did not know how to preserve it from the destruction which Allah willed.

And people still ask: why did the ancient Egyptians not leave their civilisational knowledge written and recorded in steps that later humanity could understand?

﴿And you dwelt in the dwellings of those who wronged themselves, and it became clear to you how We dealt with them, and We set forth for you the parables.﴾ (Ibrahim).

That is: the Truth, the Exalted, here makes clear that His will in sending punishment has become evident before those who were contemporaries of the message of Muhammad (ﷺ), in the dwellings of the peoples who came before them and disbelieved in the messages of the messengers; and the Truth, the Exalted, had previously set forth for them parables through these people and what happened to them. A parable is coined by Allah so that a tangible thing may bring close to minds an abstract thing.

1 Qatadah said: people dwelt in the dwellings of the people of Noah, 'Ad and Thamud, and many generations between them of the nations that perished. [al-Durr al-Manthur 5/52].
2 al-Ahqaf: the dwelling places of the people of 'Ad in the outskirts of the land of Yemen. A ḥaqf of sand is that which is winding, elongated, or rounded of sand. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/163] with additions.
3 al-Riḥ al-ṣarṣar: the intensely cold wind. It was said: the intensely loud one. [Lisan al-'Arab – root ṣ-r-r].
4 ḥaṣaba: he pelted him with pebbles. The ḥasib: a fierce whirlwind that pelts you with pebbles so that it destroys you. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/156].
5 Iram: the name of a tribe, of which 'Ad was one—and it was said it is a large city of theirs—and al-Kindi claimed in his book Fada'il Misr that it is the city of Alexandria. His saying (dhat al-'imad) indicates that it is a civilisation with lofty buildings. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/18].

Al-Sha'rawi's Commentary (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on Surah 14, verse 46:

The word of the Truth continues after that:

﴿And they have indeed plotted their plot, and with Allah is their plot, though their plot was such that the mountains would be moved thereby.﴾ [46]

Al-makr (plotting) – as we know – is the scheming of a deception concealed in hidden secrecy, and it is derived from the shajara makmura (the concealed tree), meaning the tree that covers itself. In the large gardens we see a tree the size of a finger, which is entwined around another large tree. You cannot distinguish one of its leaves, nor attribute that leaf to the place from which it emerged, or to which branch of the twining tree, unless you pull it away from around the tree that it coils around.

Whoever plots in secret is in fact bearing witness against himself to cowardice, weakness and inability to face (his opponent) openly. It may be fitting to plot against an equal of yours; but to plot against the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting, from Whom nothing on earth or in heaven is hidden, that is failure itself.

Therefore the Truth, may He be exalted, says, in response to that:

﴿And Allah is the best of planners﴾ [Al 'Imran: 54].

And He said about the plotting of these people:

﴿And the evil plot does not encompass except its own people﴾ [Fatir: 43].

We know that when we attribute a quality to Allah, we take it within the frame of:

﴿There is nothing like unto Him...﴾ [al-Shura: 11].

And it is customary that we attribute every act of Allah to good, as in His saying, may He be glorified:

﴿And You are the best of the inheritors﴾ [al-Anbiya': 89].

﴿And Allah is the best of planners﴾ [Al 'Imran: 54].

And His saying here:

﴿And they have indeed plotted their plot...﴾ [Ibrahim: 46].

That is: they established plotting suited to their stratagem, their thinking and their power. When the Truth, may He be exalted, confronts that, He will confront it with what suits His absolute power and ability. He, may He be exalted, knew from eternity what they would plot, and left them in their plotting.

The victories of messages depend on the strength of the one sent and his followers, and they confront opponents who are the very reason for the existence of the message; for they have filled the earth with corruption, and they wish to preserve the corruption that secures their authority. The new religion will shatter their sovereignty and shake it. Therefore they must spare no effort in attempting scheming and entrapment of the Messenger in order to eliminate the message.

They tried this through confrontation at the time when Islam was in its beginning: they seized the weak ones who had embraced Islam and began to torture them, yet not one of them turned back from the religion.

They tried war, so Allah granted victory to those who believed, and nothing remained for them but plotting. And He, may He be exalted, says:

﴿And [remember] when those who disbelieved plotted against you to restrain you or kill you or expel you. They plot, but Allah plots. And Allah is the best of planners﴾ [al-Anfal: 30].

They tried to corrupt the first cell of faith, which is Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ﷺ, and they thought that if they succeeded in that, the message would collapse. So they tried to buy him with wealth, but they did not succeed.

They tried to buy him with lordship and kingship, but they did not succeed, and he said his famous saying: "By Allah, if they placed the sun in my right hand and the moon in my left, on condition that I abandon this matter until Allah makes it manifest, or I perish in it, I would not abandon it." [1]

Then they resolved to kill him and to distribute his blood among the tribes, and they took from every tribe a young man to strike Muhammad ﷺ with swords in one blow as one man. But he ﷺ migrated that night, and thus their plotting did not succeed:

﴿And they have indeed plotted their plot, and with Allah is their plot...﴾ [Ibrahim: 46].

That is: He, may He be exalted, knows their plotting.

The Truth, may He be exalted, continues, saying:

﴿Though their plot was such that the mountains would be moved thereby﴾ [Ibrahim: 46].

That is: be reassured, O Muhammad. Even if their plot could remove mountains, they will not reach you. The mountains were the most mighty of created things in the eyes of the Arabs; so even if their plot were so severe that mountains would be moved by it, they will not prevail against you, O Messenger of Allah, nor will they shift you from your goal and your mission.

The Truth, may He be exalted, says:

﴿Had We sent down this Qur'an upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled, split apart out of fear of Allah. And these are the examples We present to people that they may reflect﴾ [al-Hashr: 21].

And if their plotting reaches such severity that mountains would be moved by it, then know that Allah is mightier in might.

[1] Ibn Hisham cited it in al-Sira al-Nabawiyya (1/266), attributed to Ibn Ishaq.

[2] Yuthbitu: meaning they wound you with a wound from which you cannot rise. Athbata fulan: his illness grew severe, or a wound fixed him so that he could not move. [Lisan al-'Arab, root th-b-t].

[3] Hayq: to befall and encompass; haqa bihi al-amr: it clung to him and became binding upon him. Al-hayq is the harm that befalls a person from what he himself did. [al-Mu'jam al-Wajiz, root h-y-q].

[4] Tasdi'  (tasdi'): scattering and splitting. Al-sad': a crack in a hard thing. Tasadda'a: rocks being broken with force. [Lisan al-'Arab; al-Mu'jam al-Wajiz, root s-d-'].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 14, verse 47:

Then Allah, glorified is He, presents the reason why their plotting has no effect, saying:

﴿So do not think that Allah will fail to fulfil His promise to His messengers. Indeed, Allah is Almighty, Owner of retribution.﴾ (14:47)

Had their plotting had any effect or benefit, the Truth, glorified is He, would not have said that His promise to His messengers will never be broken. But their plotting is corrupt from its beginning and without effect. And He, glorified is He, is the one who said:

﴿And My word had already preceded to Our servants, the messengers, that indeed they would be those given victory, and that indeed Our soldiers would be the victorious.﴾ (37:171-173)

So the promise of Allah to His messengers cannot be broken.

Promises in the Qur'an are many. There is the promise of Satan to his allies, in confirmation of the saying of the Truth, glorified is He:

﴿Satan threatens you with poverty and orders you to immorality, while Allah promises you forgiveness from Him and bounty...﴾ (2:268)

And there is a promise from Allah to the believers:

﴿Allah has promised those among you who believe and do righteous deeds that He will surely grant them succession upon the earth...﴾ (24:55)

So if the Truth, glorified is He, does not break His promise to the followers of the Messenger, would He break His promise to the Messenger himself?

Certainly not, because the promise of Allah in its absolute sense is fulfilled, so how much more so when it is made to the messengers and the believers? The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, says:

﴿Indeed, We will surely support Our messengers and those who believe in the life of this world and on the day when the witnesses stand.﴾ (40:51)

Victory requires the defeat of the opposing side, and victory requires a quality suited to it. The suitable qualities are that it proceeds from the Almighty who cannot be overcome, and defeat for those who disbelieve requires a quality, and the suitable quality is that defeat be achieved by the command of One who is Avenger and Compeller.

1 *Hasiba al-shay' hisbanan*: he thought it. *Fa-la tahsabanna*: i.e., do not think. [al-Mu'jam al-Wajiz, root: ḥ-s-b]
2 *Al-'Aziz*: one of the attributes and beautiful names of Allah, mighty and majestic. Al-Zajjaj said: He is the one who is unassailable, so nothing overcomes Him. Others said: He is the strong one who overcomes everything. [Lisan al-'Arab, root: ʿ-z-z]
3 Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir (1/321): (That is, He frightens you with poverty so that you hold on to what is in your hands and do not spend in pleasing Allah. And He, along with His prohibition of spending out of fear of poverty, commands you to sins, transgressions, and forbidden things, and opposing what is right.)

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 14, verse 48:

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿On the day when the earth will be changed to another earth, and the heavens as well, and they will come forth before Allah, the One, the Subduer.﴾ (48)

Here the Truth, glorified is He, warns them of the Day of Resurrection, after having depicted for them what they will claim: that the Truth would delay their reckoning, and return them to the world so that they might do righteous deeds and answer the call of the messengers.

Here He, glorified is He, makes clear that the universe which Allah created, upon which Adam descended and after him his offspring were placed, has been prepared and subjected by Him in the service of Adam and his offspring after him. They live in the universe by means of Allah's causes (asbab) extended within themselves and scattered throughout this universe for every creature of Allah, believer and disbeliever alike. Whoever takes hold of those causes is the one who prevails.

And He, glorified is He, says:

﴿Whoever desires the tilth (harth) of the Hereafter, We will increase him in his tilth; and whoever desires the tilth of this world, We will give him of it, but he will have no share in the Hereafter.﴾ (20) (al-Shura).

Thus Allah willed to grant His servants advancement in this world through causes (asbab). As for the life of the Hereafter, we live it through the Causer (al-Musabbib), and as soon as a desire for something occurs to the mind of the believer, he finds it already fulfilled.

This is a matter that does not require an earth in which the Truth has determined its sustenance (aqwat), placed in it firm mountains (rawasi), and sent down upon it water from the sky. Therefore, it is another earth and another heaven, because the earth we know is an earth of causes, and the heaven we know is a heaven of causes.

In the Paradise of the Hereafter there are no causes, so the earth must necessarily be changed, and likewise the heavens.

And His saying, the Truth:

﴿And they will come forth before Allah, the One, the Subduer.﴾ (48) (Ibrahim).

This means that there will be no one with them other than their Lord, because al-Baruz (coming forth) is emergence and confrontation.

The believer has found his Lord through belief in the unseen in his worldly life, and he believes in Him and in all that came from Him, such as the establishment of the Hour and the existence of Paradise and Hell.

All of us remember the hadith of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with one of the Companions when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked him: "How did you wake up?" The Companion said: "I woke up a true believer in Allah." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "Every truth has a reality; what is the reality of your faith?" The Companion said: "My soul has turned away from the world, so that its gold and its clods are equal to me" – that is, gold equals dust – "and it is as if I see the people of Paradise in Paradise enjoying bliss, and the people of the Fire in the Fire being punished." The noble Messenger ﷺ said to him: "You have known, so hold fast to it."

This is the state of the believer. As for the disbeliever, his state is different. He comes forth to find Allah whom he denied, a confrontation he did not expect, and therefore the Truth, glorified is He, described His own essence here as:

﴿the One, the Subduer.﴾ (47)

And there is no other god who would say to Him, "Leave them for my sake."

In another verse He says about these people:

﴿And those who disbelieve, their deeds are like a mirage in a level plain which the thirsty one thinks is water, until, when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing, and finds Allah with him...﴾ (39) (al-Nur).

That is: he is taken by surprise by such a situation for which he had not prepared.

And His saying:

﴿the One, the Subduer.﴾ (48) (Ibrahim).

That is: the One able to subdue the creature against its will.

1 Baruzu Allah: all creation came out of their graves to Allah. [Tafsir Ibn Kathir (2/544)]. Al-buruz means appearance and emergence. And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And you see the earth laid bare...﴾ (47) (al-Kahf), meaning apparent, without mountain, hill or sand. [Lisan al-Arab, root b-r-z].
2 Al-harth: reward and share. Harth al-dunya: its acquisition. [Lisan al-Arab, root h-r-th].
3 He is al-Harith ibn Malik al-Ansari. Mentioned by Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani in (al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba) (1/343), and he attributed the hadith to Ibn al-Mubarak in al-Zuhd.
4 Cited by al-Haythami in Majma' al-Zawa'id (1/57), and he attributed it to al-Tabarani in al-Kabir, from the hadith of al-Harith ibn Malik al-Ansari.
5 Al-saraab: what one sees at midday in open land as if it were water, and it is not water. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/308]. Al-qay'a is the plural of qa', the flat, wide, level land in which the mirage occurs. [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 3/296].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 14, verse 49:

He, glory be to Him, says after that:

﴿And you will see the criminals that Day bound together in shackles,﴾ (49)

The mujrim (criminal) is one who has committed a sin, and here it refers to one who has committed the greatest sin, which is disbelief in Allah, and after him those who have committed sins below disbelief. You will see them all gathered together, some with others, in a qarn (a rope or chain by which they are bound).

The asfad are the plural of safad, which is the shackle placed on the leg, similar to the khulkhal (anklet). There are those who are shackled with the asfad, i.e., on their legs, and there are those who are bound with ghulul (iron collars), i.e., their hands are placed in chains, and those chains are fastened around their necks as well.

Every people of a particular crime are bound by a single tie, for the people of each crime are, during the life of this world, generally united by affection and sympathy. Here, however, you will find them estranged and hostile; each one denounces the other, each one contends with and harasses the other, and each one displays his enmity toward him, in confirmation of the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him:

﴿The intimate friends that Day will be enemies to one another, except the righteous.﴾ (67) (Az-Zukhruf).

It is as if each of them tortures the other before they all taste the great punishment.

Therefore we find them saying:

﴿Our Lord, show us those who misled us from among the jinn and mankind that we may put them under our feet so that they will be among the lowest.﴾ (29) (Fussilat).

And they say:

﴿Our Lord, indeed we obeyed our masters and our elders, and they led us astray from the way. Our Lord, give them double the punishment and curse them with a great curse.﴾ (67-68) (Al-Ahzab).

1 Muqarranin: bound and shackled together with one another. And al-asfad: shackles. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/378].
2 Ibn Manzur said in Lisan al-Arab, entry: n-k-f: (In the Nawadir al-A'rab: "tanakafa al-rajulan al-kalam" when they exchange words) i.e., this one returns it to that one, and they exchange reproaches with words.
3 Al-Akhilla': plural of khalil, which is the sincere friend. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/208].

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary continues describing the state of these sinners. The Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Their garments of pitch, and the Fire covering their faces.﴾ [14:50]

"Sarabil" (سرابيل) is the plural of "sirbal" (سِرْبال), which is what is closest to the body, and what we call in our time a "qamis" (shirt). If the sirbal is of pitch, then it is black, biting, foul-smelling, and quick to catch fire; these are the qualities of pitch, which is a substance that oozes from some trees of the desert, and these are its properties. They use it to treat camels for mange.

Allah, glory be to Him, often strikes the parable with an image close to the mind, from among those which the Arab sees in his environment.

Concerning them, the Truth, glory be to Him, also says:

﴿And the Fire covers their faces.﴾ [14:50] (Ibrahim).

When a person is exposed to something that threatens to destroy him, the first thing he tries to protect is his face, because the face is the most honourable thing in a human being. So what of when the faces of the disbelievers are covered by the Fire? Merely imagining that is painful.

And He, glory be to Him, says in another verse:

﴿Is one who shields with his face from the terrible punishment on the Day of Resurrection...?﴾ [39:24] (Az-Zumar).

It is as though each of them, from the intensity of the torment, tries to ward off this punishment with his face. Thus we find various feelings of this punishment, and it is most painful.

He, glory be to Him, says in another place:

﴿The Day they will be dragged into the Fire upon their faces...﴾ [54:48] (Al-Qamar).

Thus we find that the face has come in more than one form among the forms of this punishment.

Footnote 1: Qitran (القطران): a black, viscous liquid substance, extracted from wood and coal and the like by dry distillation, used to preserve wood from rot and iron from rust. [al-Mu'jam al-Wajiz, entry: qatara].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 14, verse 51:

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says after that:

﴿That Allah may recompense every soul for what it has earned. Indeed, Allah is swift in reckoning.﴾ (14:51)

Recompense is a natural matter in existence. Even those who do not believe in a god, and who run the movement of their lives by legislation of their own making, have set for themselves laws of recompense that define every crime and the appropriate punishment for it.

Naturally, it is not strange that the Creator of the universe should set a system of recompense, reward and punishment. Had the Truthful, glorified is He, not set a system of recompense by reward and punishment, every corrupter would have attained his aim from his corruption, and the people of values would have felt that they had been deceived in this life.

And since recompense is a natural matter, there is no injustice in it, for it proceeds from the One who said:

﴿Today no soul will be wronged.. (40:17)﴾ (Ghafir).

The Truthful, glorified is He, does not requite with severe recompense except for a severe crime.

His saying, glorified is He:

﴿That Allah may recompense every soul for what it has earned.. (14:51)﴾ (Ibrahim).

means that the believer or the disbeliever will meet the recompense of what he did, whether reward or punishment.

Al-kasb (earning), as we know, is to take something in addition to the principal. So when you deprive yourself of something in this world, you will take a recompense, which is reward and what exceeds the principal.

Whoever earns an evil deed will receive a punishment for it. It is said "kasaba al-sayyi'ah" (he earned the evil deed), and it is not said "iktasabahā" (he acquired it), because his committing of the evil deed has become a behavioural habit, and he rejoices in committing it. Recompense is therefore necessary, recompense requires reckoning, and reckoning requires a scale.

The believer may say: "I believe in my Lord, and my Lord will not wrong anyone." We say: the purpose of the scale is the establishment of proof. That is why He, glorified is He, says:

﴿As for him whose scales are heavy, (6) he will be in a pleasant life. (7)﴾ (al-Qari'ah).

And He also says:

﴿And as for him whose scales are light, (8) his mother will be an abyss. (9)﴾ (al-Qari'ah).

The rational division in the scale is clear: sometimes it is (heavy, thaqulat) and sometimes (light, khaffat). As for one whose two pans are balanced, his condition is explained by the surah of al-A'raf, in which the Truthful, glorified is He, says:

﴿And upon the heights (al-A'raf)(2) are men who recognize each by his mark (sīmāhum).. (7:46)﴾ (al-A'raf).

Since the Truthful, glorified is He, will reckon every soul for what it has earned, someone may think that this will take time. Therefore He, glorified is He, follows with:

﴿Indeed, Allah is swift in reckoning. (14:51)﴾ (Ibrahim).

to show us that He, glorified is He, will reckon all creation from Adam until the Hour is established, with a speed that befits His absolute power.

When people asked the Imam ʿAli, may Allah honour his face, "How will Allah reckon all creation at once?", he gave a clear and sufficient answer, saying: "As He provides for them all at once."

1 That is: he will fall headlong, head first, into the fire of Hell. He expressed it as "his mother," meaning his brain. Qatadah said: he will fall into the fire on his head. [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 4/543].
2 The People of al-A'raf are a people whose good deeds and bad deeds were equal, so their bad deeds kept them from Paradise, and their good deeds kept them from the Fire, so they stood there upon the wall until Allah decides concerning them. [Mentioned by Ibn Kathir in his tafsir 2/216].
3 As-Sawma: with a damma, a mark. Ibn ʿAbbas said: they recognize the people of Paradise by the whiteness of their faces and the people of the Fire by the blackness of their faces. [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 2/218].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 14, verse 52:

He, glorified is He, says after that:

﴿This is a message (balagh) for mankind, that they may be warned thereby, and that they may know that He is but one God, and that people of understanding may take heed.﴾

This verse is the seal of the conclusion (misk al-khitam), for it has concentrated the call: a message issued from God so that His Messenger, who was supported with the miracle, may convey it, so as to carry the way of life (manhaj al-hayah) to man, the vicegerent (khalifah) on earth.

When the laws of the movement of life are issued for man, the vicegerent on earth, who was created by God, no one may add to them by way of completion or perfection, because He who created is He who legislated. This matter must be before the mind of every accountable (mukallaf) person.

When you read the wise saying:

﴿This is a message for mankind..﴾ (Ibrahim).

you find that it carries an indication to the whole Qur'an, for the scope of the message is everything that came down from God.

And the word of the Truth, glorified is He:

﴿This is a message for mankind..﴾ (Ibrahim).

has given us what the modern legal text gives, for the modern legal text makes clear that there is no punishment except by a text that criminalizes the act, and the text must be announced to all people. That is why laws are published in the official gazette of the state, so that no one may say: "I was unaware that the law had been issued."

We all know that the Truth, glorified is He, has said:

﴿And We would never punish until We send a messenger.﴾ (15) (al-Isra').

So the task of the Messenger, then, is the conveying from God of the way of life that safeguards the movement of life.

He, glorified is He, says concerning the task of the Messenger:

﴿But upon you is only the conveying, and upon Us is the reckoning.﴾ (40) (al-Ra'd).

He, glorified is He, says:

﴿Those who convey the messages of God and fear Him, and fear none but God.. ﴾ (39) (al-Ahzab).

And the Truth, glorified is He, says on the tongue of the Messenger(1):

﴿I have conveyed to you the messages of my Lord..﴾ (93) (al-A'raf).

And He also says:

﴿I have conveyed to you that with which I was sent..﴾ (57) (Hud).

Thus there is no argument for one who says: "I was seized for a sin I did not know to be a sin at the time of being charged." There is no argument for one who speaks such a word, because the Truth, glorified is He, says in the same verse:

﴿And that they may be warned thereby..﴾ (52) (Ibrahim).

Warning (al-indhar) is the frightening of a person with an evil that will befall him before its time, so as to make clear to you the horror of disobedience; likewise, good tidings (al-tabshir) is an alerting to a good that is coming but has not yet arrived in its time, so that you may prepare to receive it.

The word of the Truth, glorified is He:

﴿This is a message for mankind..﴾ (Ibrahim).

includes good tidings also, but it emphasizes and affirms afterward in His saying:

﴿And that they may be warned thereby..﴾ (Ibrahim).

because the loss will fall upon the perpetrator of sins.

And I say: the warning here is a blessing, because it reminds a person so that he does not proceed to commit a sin or disobedience. When the outcome (maghabbah(2)) of evil action is presented to a person, it is as though you are presenting him with a blessing, and bestowing upon him a favor and a kindness.

He, glorified is He, continues:

﴿And that they may know that He is but one God..﴾ (Ibrahim).

This is the first doctrinal matter, which comes at the summit of all matters: He is one God, from whose command we all proceed, for the important matter in this life is that the movements of living beings converge and support one another, not that they contradict one another.

No structure rises if, when you build one day, another comes and demolishes what you built.

The task of the movement of life is that we perform our duty as vicegerents of God on earth, by our talents being mutually reinforcing, not conflicting, so that the whole human society moves in one direction, because it proceeds from one God and one command.

When the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿And this is a message for mankind..﴾ (Ibrahim).

He defines for us the foundation of the religion: after receiving it from the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, each one who hears it must convey it to one who has not heard it.

For this reason the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: (May God make radiant the face of a man who hears my saying, retains it, and conveys it to one who has not heard it.)(4)

This is so that the chain of conveying remains connected. If a people is not informed, the burden falls on the one who failed to convey, and by that he deprives himself of the honor of following the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him. Whoever knows a ruling of the religion, what is required of him is to convey it to others, just as the Truth, glorified is He, required of His Messenger that he convey His rulings.

And the Truth, glorified is He, is the One who said:

﴿And thus We made you a middle nation (ummah wasatan)(5), that you may be witnesses over mankind and the Messenger may be a witness over you..﴾ (143) (al-Baqarah).

Thus the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, bore witness that he had conveyed to you, and it remains for every Muslim who knows a ruling of the religion to convey it to one who does not know it; for he may benefit from it more than he himself does, and after hearing the ruling he may act upon it, whereas the one who conveyed the ruling to him may not act upon it.

For this reason the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: (Many a one to whom something is conveyed is more retentive than the one who hears it.)(6)

For this reason I always say: beware of confusing the information that is told to you with the conduct of the one who told it to you. Let us hear the poet who said:

Take my knowledge and do not rely on my deeds,
and gather the fruit and leave the stick for firewood.

Thus the Muslim bears the responsibility of conveying what he knows of the rulings of the religion to those who have no knowledge of them, so that the message remains connected. We all know that the Truth, glorified is He, has said:

﴿You are the best nation brought forth for mankind, enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong..﴾ (110) (Al 'Imran).

That is: you, O nation of Muhammad, have taken up the task of the prophets.

And because the message came from God to the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, and the Messenger is trustworthy in conveying it, therefore conflicting commands cannot proceed from the Wise One. Conflict arises only from a difference in the commander or from the lack of wisdom in the commander. Let us examine carefully the word of the Truth, glorified is He:

﴿And that they may know that He is but one God..﴾ (Ibrahim).

The word (one, wahid) came to prevent even the mere conception of partnership; there is none like Him, and He is One who is not composed of parts, so He has no organs resembling the organs of humans, for if He had organs He would in His essence need His parts, and this is not valid and cannot be imagined regarding God, glorified and exalted is He.

This is the fundamental matter which the people of understanding who receive this message grasp. "People of understanding" (ulu al-albab) is plural, and the singular of (albab) is (lubb), and the lubb of a thing is the reality of its essence, for the husk exists to protect this kernel, and what is protected is always more precious than the thing that encloses it to preserve it.

Thus the people of understanding are the human beings who receive the matter of faith with their minds, and who set their minds in motion to remember it constantly, for the preoccupations, pleasures and desires of life may divert a person from the way; therefore the Truth, glorified is He, said:

﴿And that people of understanding may take heed..﴾ (Ibrahim).

That is: those possessed of minds remember that God is One, the Unique, so there is no god but Him. Therefore He, glorified is He, bore witness to Himself before any other being bore witness to Him, and said:

﴿God bears witness that there is no god but He..﴾ (18) (Al 'Imran).

This is the witness of the Essence to the Essence. He adds, glorified is He:

﴿And the angels and those of knowledge..﴾ (18).

The witness of the angels is the witness of direct confrontation which they experienced, and the witness of the people of understanding is the witness of inference.

The Truth, glorified is He, also bore witness to His Messenger Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, that he is a messenger; and likewise the Messenger bore witness to himself, for he says, as we all say: (I bear witness that there is no god but God, and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of God).

Thus upon the people of understanding lies a task: to remember and to remind that He is one God, the Unique.

(1) The Messenger here is Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, for God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Those who denied Shu'ayb, as though they had never dwelt therein; those who denied Shu'ayb, they were the losers. So he turned away from them and said, "O my people, I have certainly conveyed to you the messages of my Lord and advised you, so how should I grieve over a disbelieving people?"﴾ (92-93) (al-A'raf).

(2) Al-ghibb of anything: its consequence and its end. Likewise al-maghabbah. [al-Mu'jam al-Wajiz, root: gh-b-b].

(3) Nadara Allah wajhahu: He made his face bright/blessed. Al-nadrah: blessing, beauty and radiance. Al-Hasan al-Mu'addib said: this is not beauty of the face; rather its meaning is: may God beautify his face in his character, i.e., his standing and rank. [Lisan al-Arab, root: n-d-r].

(4) Recorded by Ahmad in his Musnad (1/437), al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan (2657, 2658), Ibn Majah in his Sunan (232), and al-Humaydi in his Musnad (1/47), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him.

(5) Ummah wasatan: that is, an excellent, virtuous nation, for al-wasat is the best of two extremes.  [al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/336].

(6) The full hadith: (May God make radiant the face of a man who hears my saying, retains it, and conveys it to one who has not heard it..), the hadith, whose takhrij has been mentioned earlier on page (7623).
